objects.name: The disarmament of Chechnya: a military operation with artillery shelling and bombing of auls (1925)
objects.description: By 1925 Soviet power had stood in Chechnya for its fifth year and remained largely nominal: five years of Sovietization (campaign C1176) - revkoms (revolutionary committees) instead of elected Soviets, arrests of sheikhs, two partial disarmaments - had not given Moscow control over the people, imam Nazhmuddin Gotsinsky, the spiritual head of the armed resistance in Dagestan and Chechnya, was sheltering in the mountains, and the profile of the Mountain district drawn up by the staff of the future operation admitted: "Beyond the Sharo-Argun Soviet power does not exist"(Citation: Чечня. Политическая и общественная обстановка. 1920-30 гг. 2021). Moscow, meanwhile, was steering a course toward taking power away from the autonomies - historian T. U. Elbuzdukayeva writes: "The unceasing banditry and insurgent movements in the North Caucasus were perceived by the Moscow authorities as a convincing argument in favor of its centralizing efforts, the process of transferring autonomous sovereignty from Caucasian into Moscow hands"(Citation: Хроника первого разоружения Чечни 2015). The operation of 1925 became that course in action: the USSR took away the weapons of Chechnya's population with the forces of the army and the OGPU (the political police, a predecessor of today's FSB) - from 25 August the troops passed through 242 settlements, shelled 101 of them with [artillery] guns and machine guns, bombed 16 from aircraft, arrested more than 300 people and shot nearly all of them without trial. Under the guise of maneuvers the troops entered the oblast, surrounded aul after aul, convened the village assembly, presented an ultimatum to surrender weapons according to a ready-made quota, and opened fire on the settlement if it was not met; of the aims Elbuzdukayeva writes: as the centers of the operation the staff had designated in advance the mountain societies "where N. Gotsinsky [the head of the resistance] was presumed to be"(Citation: Хроника первого разоружения Чечни 2015). The instruction of 4 August 1925, approved by Uborevich, commander of the North Caucasus Military District (SKVO), prescribed, should the ultimatum not be met, opening artillery fire on the settlement for ten minutes, and allowed repeating it several times(Citation: О подготовке к операции по разоружению и борьбе с бандитизмом в Чечне 2022). The deception, too, was assigned by document: by an order of 31 July 1925 the staff of the Workers' and Peasants' Red Army (RKKA) approved Uborevich's maneuvers in Chechnya and with the same document assigned the disarmament: "At the same time," the order said, "taking advantage of the concentration of a significant number of troops on the territory of Chechnya (the district of the forthcoming maneuvers), the command of the SKVO, in coordination with the PPOGPU [the plenipotentiary representation of the OGPU] in the North Caucasus, plans to carry out a disarmament and a removal of the bandit element, which by a number of political indications is highly timely"(Citation: Повстанческое движение на Северном Кавказе в 1920-1925 годах 2013). The sanction was given by Stalin personally: in July 1925 Mikoyan, secretary of the North Caucasus krai committee of the party(Citation: ЦК РКП(б)-ВКП(б) и национальный вопрос. Кн. 1. 1918-1933 гг. 2005), met him in Sochi and after the conversation telegraphed to Molotov in Moscow: "The political situation in Chechnya has become aggravated. Stalin has given his personal consent to the necessity of the operation"(Citation: Хроника первого разоружения Чечни 2015). Many years later Mikoyan summed it up in his memoirs: "This operation fundamentally cleared the air of Chechnya"(Citation: Так было: Размышления о минувшем 1999).

objects.name: Collectivization of Chechnya (1927-1936)
objects.description: In 1927, after stripping the Chechen people of their weapons (campaign C1177), the USSR began forcibly merging the peasant households of Chechnya into kolkhozes - collective farms controlled by the Russian state ("collectivization"). That same spring the USSR broke off relations with Great Britain and expected war - and its first move was to purge the Chechen "rear": in the summer of 1927 the OGPU (the political police, a predecessor of today's FSB) arrested sixteen religious authorities across Chechnya. Yevdokimov, the OGPU plenipotentiary in the North Caucasus, recorded in a secret report: "The days of military danger of the summer period unusually inspired the Chechen musduh [Muslim clergy] in the sense of bold and open agitation for aid to external forces, for the preparation of an uprising"(Citation: Доклад Евдокимова о политическом состоянии национальных областей 1928). Thus the empire ascribed to the Chechens an uprising that did not exist; the real uprisings it provoked itself two years later - with kolkhozes, devastation and the closing of mosques. On 30 January 1930 the supreme organ of the occupation power (the "Politburo of the TsK VKP(b)") adopted a secret resolution "On measures for the liquidation of kulak households in districts of wholesale collectivization"; "kulaks" was what the colonizers called peasants they deemed "well-off". The Politburo resolved to ruin on average three to five percent of peasant households across the USSR and divided their owners into three categories: the first - to concentration camps, up to execution by shooting; the second - to exile in remote places; the third - to resettlement on the worst plots within their own district; across the country it ordered 60 thousand people sent to the camps and 150 thousand expelled from their land, with 6-8 thousand and 20 thousand assigned to the North Caucasus with Dagestan. The Politburo entrusted the reprisal against the first and second categories to the OGPU, and on 2 February 1930 deputy chairman of the OGPU Yagoda signed order No. 44/21 "On measures for the liquidation of the kulaks as a class"(Citation: Трагедия советской деревни. Коллективизация и раскулачивание. Том 2. Ноябрь 1929 - декабрь 1930 2000). From thousands of Chechen families whom the colonizer deemed well-off it took away voting rights, livestock and land, and expelled the people themselves beyond the borders of their native region. The USSR struck at the religious life of the Chechens as well: it squeezed out the sharia courts - they decided Chechens' cases by Islamic law, - stripped those courts of treasury money and closed mosques. The Nokhchi did not submit and rose in arms three times: in December 1929 Shali, Goity and Benoy revolted, in the spring of 1930 - the mountain okrugs, including Galanchozh, in March 1932 - the Nozhay-Yurt district. All three times the USSR sent troops with artillery and aviation against the insurgents; the toll of the year 1932 alone, from historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov: "the number of killed reached 333, of wounded - 150. The units of the Red Army and the operational groups of the GPU lost in all 27 men killed..."(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005). After the uprising of 1932 the OGPU fabricated the "Chechen nationalist center" - an underground organization that did not exist: thus the empire passed the uprisings off as the fruit of a secret conspiracy(Citation: Убийство чечено-ингушского народа. Народоубийство в СССР 1952). In the case of the "center" the OGPU arrested up to 3 thousand Chechens(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005), shot five captured leaders of the uprising and the "members of the center", whom the Chechen historian A. G. Avtorkhanov names one by one; the count of the rank-and-file shot is unknown(Citation: Убийство чечено-ингушского народа. Народоубийство в СССР 1952). Belov, commander of the occupation troops of the North Caucasus Military District (SKVO), wrote in the district command's secret report to the krai committee of the party (the "North Caucasus kraikom VKP(b)") on the results of the military operation of spring 1930: "The causes of the outbreak are... The gravest errors of the old party leadership of the oblast, which pursued a completely incorrect line of wholesale collectivization, without regard for the particularities and the level of development of the national oblast", and further listed: "The administrative imposition of kolkhozes, attempts at collectivization in the mountain districts, the incorrect disenfranchisement of middle peasants, and in a number of cases of poor peasants as well... the attempt at the administrative closing of mosques"(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011). Historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov named this policy in the title of their chapter: "The collectivization of agriculture. The enserfment of the peasantry by the state"(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005).

objects.name: The Great Terror in Chechen-Ingushetia (1937-1940)
objects.description: By 1937 Chechnya had been through disarmament (campaign C1177) and the forced merging of peasant households into kolkhozes ("collectivization") with punitive expeditions against insurgent auls (campaign C1178). In 1934 the colonizer merged the oblast with Ingushetia into the united Chechen-Ingush Autonomous Oblast, and in 1936 renamed it the Chechen-Ingush Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic (ChIASSR); today the occupier calls these lands the Chechen Republic and the Republic of Ingushetia within Russia. Through this republic, as through other parts of the USSR, passed the Great Terror: that is what historians call the mass arrests and executions of 1937-1938, for which Moscow assigned each republic and oblast its own number. The repressions began with the resolution of the supreme organ of the occupation power (the "Politburo of the TsK VKP(b)") "On anti-Soviet elements" of 2 July 1937, signed by Stalin(Citation: Новая волна репрессий против крестьянства и других слоев населения в республиках Северного Кавказа в 1937-1938 гг. 2014). On 11 July 1937 the Politburo, by a separate decision, approved the number of people to be shot in the republic - separately for peasants whom the colonizer deemed "well-off" ("kulaks") and for "criminals"; the historian G. I. Kakagasanov cites it thus: "kulaks - 862 pers., criminals - 555 pers."(Citation: Новая волна репрессий против крестьянства и других слоев населения в республиках Северного Кавказа в 1937-1938 гг. 2014). On 30 July Yezhov, the People's Commissar (minister) of Internal Affairs of the USSR, issued operational order No. 00447 "On the operation to repress former kulaks, criminals and other anti-Soviet elements"; for the ChIASSR it records: 500 people - to be shot (the order's "first category"), 1,500 - to be confined in camps (the "second category")(Citation: Приказ НКВД СССР № 00447 1937). Already by mid-August 1937 the arrested were more numerous than recorded in the order, and on 1 March 1938 Moscow assigned the republic a new number - 10,108 people ordered arrested and convicted(Citation: Политические репрессии в Чечне 1920-1930-х годов 2019). Historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov write: "by various estimates, in the '30s - early '40s no fewer than 30-40 thousand Chechens and Ingush became victims of the Stalinist terror"(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005). The case of the "bourgeois-nationalist center" - 137 former senior officials of the republic - the Chekist investigators, as the Chechen historian A. G. Avtorkhanov writes, spent three years fabricating; the military tribunal tried the arrested in 1940(Citation: Убийство чечено-ингушского народа. Народоубийство в СССР 1952).

objects.name: "Bombs Rained Down on the Auls": Repression and Air Strikes on Mountain Chechnya on the Eve of the Deportation (1941-1942)
objects.description: In the autumn of 1941 the Second World War was underway: Germany was advancing on the USSR, and the front was moving toward the Caucasus. The USSR was taking Chechens to its war: during the first mass mobilization, from 29 August to 2 September 1941, the military commissariats took almost 8 thousand men - 269 managed to evade, and another 450 fled on the way to the dispatch point(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011). In October they took another 4.4 thousand - 362 did not report to the recruitment stations(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011). The commissariats sent up to 13 thousand more men, unfit for combat service, to the "labor army" - construction battalions(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005). Already in September 1941 the labor-army trains found themselves in the frontline zone, where more than 10 thousand of these men died(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005). The colonizer recorded as "deserters" those who fled death in the "labor army", those who evaded mobilization into it, and even those who failed to appear at a recruitment station because of disability or their own death; the Chechen historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov write: "The unfortunate citizens were forced either to hide from arrest or to pay bribes to the officials of the military commissariats and the NKVD" - and add: "Mass bribes taken from the highlanders became the everyday practice of the military commissariats"(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005). In early October 1941 the mountain villages of Chechnya rose against the collective farms and the mobilization - according to the report of the commander of the 141st Regiment of the NKVD Internal Troops (predecessors of today's Rosgvardia), Lieutenant Colonel Khalukhaev, dated 26 June 1943, the protest covered the Shatoy (Shatoevsky), Itum-Kale, Galanchozh, Cheberloy and Sharoy districts(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011). Even by the data of the secret services this was an economic protest: the population of the mountain villages "proceeded to a spontaneous division of collective-farm property" - property the colonizer had merged into collective farms during collectivization (campaign C1178); the same records charged the people with mass non-payment of taxes and evasion of mobilization; Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov likewise see "features of social protest" in the events(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005). The USSR's response was a military operation across the mountain districts, the declaration of this protest a "kulak-bandit uprising", and operational groups and NKVD troops left behind in the mountains. The historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov write that, "besides the operational groups and internal troops, three flights of combat aircraft were brought in" for the suppression, and "Bombs rained down on auls whose population did not even suspect any 'uprising'"(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005). "In the period from 30 October to 15 November 1941 the 141st rifle regiment, together with other units, crushed the c[ounter]-r[evolutionary] uprising in heavy multi-day fighting," Khalukhaev reported to Sheredega, head of the NKVD Internal Troops of the USSR(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011).

objects.name: Operation "Chechevitsa": the Total Deportation of the Chechen People and the Special Settlement Regime (1943-1949)
objects.description: On 23 February 1944 the USSR deported the entire Chechen people from their native land to Kazakhstan and Kirghizia (today's Kyrgyzstan). The deportation was total - the numbers show it: the 1939 census counted 387.5 thousand Chechens in Checheno-Ingushetia(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011), and by 1 March 1944 the Soviet NKVD (predecessor of today's FSB) reported 387,229 deported Chechens - 478,479 people together with the Ingush(Citation: Из истории насильственного выселения чеченцев и ингушей: к 80-летию депортации 2024). The colonizer named this expulsion Operation "Chechevitsa" ("Lentil"): historian P. M. Polian writes that already in November 1943 Deputy People's Commissar (Minister) of Internal Affairs Chernyshev was discussing with the heads of regional NKVD directorates "questions connected with the planned Operation 'Chechevitsa' - the deportation of some 0.5 million Vainakhs (Chechens and Ingush)"(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011). The supreme organ of the occupation authority (the "Politburo of the TsK VKP(b)") had been discussing the deportation a year before the announced pretext - the accusation that the people had aided the Germans: on 11 February 1943 the talk was already about timing, and Stalin "leaned toward the second proposal" - to deport after the Germans had been driven from the Caucasus(Citation: Из истории насильственного выселения чеченцев и ингушей: к 80-летию депортации 2024). Albogachiev, the former People's Commissar (Minister) of Internal Affairs of the republic, admitted in 1963: "I repeat once more - there were no grounds whatsoever for the deportation of the Chechens and Ingush. This was confirmed by Beria himself during his trial in 1953"(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005). Historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov write: "All of the above allows us to qualify with confidence the deportation, in this case of the Chechens and Ingush, as the gravest of crimes - genocide"(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005). Historian D. A. Khozhaev writes: "the second attempt to annihilate the Chechens was undertaken in 1944, when the entire people was driven from its native land and deported to Central Asia and Kazakhstan"(Citation: Чеченцы в Русско-Кавказской войне 1998). On 26 April 1991 the colonizer acknowledged the genocide by its own law - Article 2 of the RSFSR law "On the Rehabilitation of Repressed Peoples" states: "Repressed peoples are recognized to be those peoples... against whom, on grounds of national or other identity, a state-level policy of slander and genocide was carried out, accompanied by their forcible resettlement..."(Citation: О реабилитации репрессированных народов 1991). In 2004 the European Parliament recognized in a resolution: "the deportation of the entire Chechen people to Central Asia on 23 February 1944 on the orders of Stalin constitutes an act of genocide within the meaning of the Fourth Hague Convention of 1907 and the Convention for the Prevention and Repression of the Crime of Genocide adopted by the UN General Assembly on 9 December 1948"(Citation: Рекомендация Европейского парламента по отношениям ЕС-Россия 2004). In its resolution of 18 October 2022 the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine condemned "the international crimes committed by the russian federation during the first (1994-1996) and second (1999-2009) wars against the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria, the policy of genocide of the Chechen people, following the criminal actions of the tsarist regime of 1817-1864 and of the soviet authorities of 1944"(Citation: Заява Верховної Ради України про засудження збройної агресії проти Чеченської Республіки Ічкерія та геноциду Чеченського народу 2022).

objects.name: "Exiled Forever": Life in Special Settlement and Return to an Occupied Homeland (1949-1965)
objects.description: After the deportation of the Chechens in 1944 (campaign C1180) the occupiers took over their homes, auls and fields. By 1952 there were more than a million of them on the lands of the deported peoples of the North Caucasus(Citation: Убийство чечено-ингушского народа. Народоубийство в СССР 1952). By its decree of 26 November 1948 the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR had already declared the exile eternal: the Chechens and Ingush were "exiled forever," with up to 20 years of hard labor for escape(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005). The exile itself was built as a prison without walls. The secret police admitted: "In 1949 a series of measures was carried out to track down and detain fugitives, as well as to establish a strict regime in the places of settlement"(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011). Under the resolution of the government of the USSR of 8 January 1945, "any unauthorized absence of a deportee beyond the bounds of the resettlement district served by the special commandant's office shall be regarded as escape and shall entail criminal liability," and that district was at times limited to a few streets in a town or a single village soviet(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011). Those whom the agency listed among the "malicious evaders of work on the collective farms" faced 8 years of imprisonment(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011), and in July 1952 the occupiers' court sent ten religious mentors and their followers to the camps for terms of up to 25 years with confiscation of property(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011). The "eternal" term of exile rested on Stalin's decrees. The tightening of 1948-1949 followed his late-1940s course of crushing any self-reliance, and to the secret police, which demanded that fugitives be jailed indiscriminately, he handed as a reward both the supervision of the special settlers and the disposal of their labor(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011). After his death the term of the Chechens' exile became a matter of bargaining between agencies: in the summer of 1953 a department of the Central Committee of the Bolshevik party proposed removing 560,710 people from the special-settlement rolls, Chechens and Ingush among them, while the police ministry demanded that "the said categories of persons temporarily remain in special settlement"(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011); in September Kruglov, Minister of Internal Affairs of the USSR, asked Malenkov, chairman of the Council of Ministers of the USSR, to keep the Chechens and Ingush in settlement for another five years, deeming their release from surveillance premature. No decision on his memorandum was ever taken(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011). The empire did not return the seized lands even when it let the people out of exile: by its decree of 16 July 1956 the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR lifted the special-settlement regime from the Chechen people (forced residence in Kazakhstan and Kirghizia under the surveillance of commandants' offices) - and in the same article laid down that the lifting of restrictions "does not entail the return to them of property confiscated at deportation, and that they do not have the right to return to the places from which they were deported"(Citation: О снятии ограничений по спецпоселению с чеченцев, ингушей, карачаевцев и членов их семей 1956). The ministries explained the ban by saying the land had already been handed out. Barsukov, head of the occupier's police, reported on 26 June 1956 that housing the Chechens and Ingush in their districts "is not possible," because "these districts are settled by migrants from the central oblasts of the RSFSR"(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011), while Dudorov, Minister of Internal Affairs of the USSR, reported to the leadership of the Bolshevik party (the "TsK KPSS"): "the possibility of restoring autonomy for the Chechens and Ingush within their former territory is a difficult matter and hardly feasible... the return of the Chechens and Ingush to their former places of residence will inevitably provoke a whole range of undesirable consequences"(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011). The people returned on their own, without waiting for permissions: already on 15 June 1957 the bureau of the regional committee of the Bolshevik party (the "Checheno-Ingush obkom of the KPSS") admitted that "more than 122 thousand Chechens and Ingush have already arrived in the republic instead of the 70 thousand provided for by the plan for 1957"(Citation: Вайнахи и имперская власть 2011), and the resettlement department of the colonial administration (the "Orgkomitet for the ChIASSR") counted in a report of 20 January 1958: under the plan 23,503 families were to resettle - 52,037 families, 201,746 people, had arrived(Citation: По решению Правительства Союза ССР 2003). "Almost a third of the adult Chechens, Ingush and Karachais (up to 80 thousand people) refused to give" the pledge renouncing their property, write historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov, "and returned home regardless of the bans"(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005). People arrived to a homeland occupied by settlers and cut down by a redrawing of borders: they had to buy their own houses back from the new owners(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005), the mountain auls remained closed, and the Ingush lands of the Tarskaya valley, where the Ingush people had taken shape, the empire did not return to the Chechens and Ingush: in 1944 it gave them to North Ossetia and, restoring the republic in 1957, left 1,600 square kilometers of black earth with Ossetia, adding to the republic in exchange 5,000 square kilometers of the sands of the Burun steppe beyond the Terek; the protests of the Chechen-Ingush delegation were rejected by the leadership of the Bolshevik party(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005). Historians reckon the outcome in shares: "by 1961 the Chechens and Ingush made up 41% of the republic's population, whereas in 1939 their share had reached 58.4%"(Citation: История Чечни в XIX-XX веках 2005).

objects.name: Regular Army
objects.description: Armed forces under direct state control.

objects.name: Moscow Patriarchate
objects.description: Religious institutions loyal to the empire, used for ideological legitimization.

objects.name: Occupation and Controlled Administrations
objects.description: External or artificially created loyal governing bodies that replace or duplicate legitimate local authority.

objects.name: Secret Police and Security Services
objects.description: Instruments of covert interference, bribery of elites, orchestration of proxy wars, interrogation, and institutional terror against dissenters. Historical incarnations: the Preobrazhensky Prikaz, the Secret Chancellery, the FSK and the FSB of Russia.

objects.name: Controlled Opposition
objects.description: Legal political parties, movements, or factions within the colonized society that are covertly or openly sponsored, directed, and comprehensively supported by the aggressor state. They are used as a proxy instrument for destabilization, for the procedural seizure of power from within, and for legitimizing external interference under the guise of a domestic political process.

objects.name: Propaganda
objects.description: A state institutional apparatus of mass ideological influence, formatting of consciousness, and cognitive control. It included specialized party structures (in particular, the agitation and propaganda departments of the Central Committee), as well as the press, the system of mass events, cinema, and literature, all fully controlled by the authorities. It was used by the aggressor to replace real history with artificial imperial-communist myths, to subject the population to total ideological indoctrination, and to deliberately cultivate a fanatical totalitarian personality type, blindly devoted to the regime and cruel toward dissenters. The propaganda machine served as the basic mechanism for legitimizing state violence and masking the policy of forced assimilation.

objects.name: Punitive Medicine and Psychiatry
objects.description: The use of the state healthcare apparatus, psychiatric clinics, and research institutes as a punitive instrument. The system of medical institutions is turned into an extension of the repressive apparatus: doctors under the control of the security services fabricate politically motivated diagnoses (for example, the nonexistent "sluggish schizophrenia"), while closed institutions are used as prisons for the indefinite isolation and drug-induced torture of dissenters (Citation: Карательная психиатрия в России: назад в СССР? 2020).

external_references.description: Карательная психиатрия в России: назад в СССР? 2020. – Riddle Russia.

objects.name: Police Apparatus
objects.description: The police apparatus provides everyday coercive and administrative control over society. The metropole needs this instrument to hold on to power, to maintain the desired order on the ground, and to keep basic records of the population, including through mechanisms of registration and restrictions on movement. From the 1600s to the present day, this system has changed only its signboards: voivode offices and investigative prikazes gave way to the city police and address bureaus in the Russian Empire. In the Soviet era, this branch of power was embodied in the vast structures of the NKVD and the MVD, and today the same supervisory and administrative function continues to be performed by the modern MVD system.

objects.name: Government
objects.description: An instrument of internal administration and institutional coercion. It comes into use once a territory has already been stripped of international subjecthood and de facto turned into an internal colony. It encompasses the work of the metropole's entire state and bureaucratic apparatus: the issuance of discriminatory laws and decrees, changes to administrative borders, systematic cultural and educational assimilation, social engineering, and the legal formalization of control (through population censuses or imitation referendums).

objects.name: Diplomacy
objects.description: An instrument of foreign-policy pressure and manipulation. It is applied by the colonizers in the international arena toward sovereign (or formally independent) states until their complete absorption. It includes negotiation processes, the imposition of enslaving treaties, the creation of legal traps, external economic blockades, international blackmail, and collusion with third countries on the partition of others' territories.

objects.name: Militarized Settlers
objects.description: An instrument of demographic and military expansion that combines military service with agricultural labor and the physical settlement of territories. It is employed by the state to create an armed buffer on the frontier, to displace Indigenous populations from their lands, and to radically reduce the cost of maintaining an army of many thousands. The settlers are shifted to self-sufficiency, bound to the land, and placed under the total control of the military command. Historical incarnations: the irregular Cossack hosts (Terek, Greben, Kuban), as well as the institution of military settlements deployed on a large scale in the Russian Empire by Alexander I under the direction of Count A. A. Arakcheyev. In introducing this system, the emperor drew on European experience: the model was the Prussian cantonal system of army recruitment (Kantonssystem), under which the country was divided into military districts and a soldier's service was combined with cultivating the land, including on the territories seized after the partition of Poland.

The Tsardom of Muscovy exploited the critical position of the Hetmanate to impose a format of subordination, refusing from the outset to take on symmetrical obligations. To the Cossacks' demand for a mutual oath the tsar's envoy answered with a refusal - by the embassy's own report, swearing on behalf of the sovereign was "a thing that has never happened and never will, and it is unbecoming for the hetman even to say such things, for every subject must swear to his sovereign"(Citation: Історія України-Руси: Т. IX 1931); Khmelnytsky had to convene the council three times in a single day, 18 (8) January 1654, yet Buturlin, citing the autocratic character of the Russian monarch's power, refused a second time(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011). The "treaty" itself was not a bilateral act: "The originals of the treaty documents have not survived. Only their copies and drafts are known"; the Ukrainian side submitted its terms "in the form of petitions to the tsar," while "the acts of the tsarist government took the form of 'grants' from the tsar"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003) - the written terms were drawn up only in Moscow in March 1654.

The "treaty" itself was not a bilateral act: "The originals of the treaty documents have not survived. Only their copies and drafts are known"; the Ukrainian side submitted its terms "in the form of petitions to the tsar," while "the acts of the tsarist government took the form of 'grants' from the tsar"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003) - the written terms were drawn up only in Moscow in March 1654.

objects.description: From the very beginning, Moscow laid an asymmetric foundation for the relationship, harshly cutting off the autonomy's international agency. Tsar Aleksei's charter (27 March 1654) directly restricted the hetman's foreign relations: "And with the Turkish sultan and the Polish king, without our tsarist majesty's decree, no relations are to be maintained"(Citation: Жалованная грамота царя Алексея Михайловича Войску Запорожскому 1654).

objects.description: As soon as political interests changed, Moscow went for a separate peace with its recent enemy – Poland – negotiating behind its Ukrainian ally's back: "The priorities at the negotiations were territorial and financial questions, as well as the terms of the election of the Russian tsar to the Polish throne"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003) – the fate of the Cossack lands became a bargaining chip in this deal. The negotiations were held at Niemieza near Vilna from August 1656; the armistice was signed on October 24(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003).

objects.description: The Tsardom of Muscovy physically and legally isolated the autonomy from participation in international politics, deciding the fate of the Cossack lands without regard for their national interests: "The plenipotentiary representatives of the Ukrainian Cossack state, headed by R. Haponenko, were not admitted to the negotiating table"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003). The hetman's request to grant the envoys mandates as full participants was "let pass unheeded" by the tsar's government: the delegates "sat idle beside the commissioners, not admitted to the official sessions"(Citation: Історія України-Руси: Т. IX 1931).

objects.description: Seeking to weaken the Hetmanate from within and prevent it from breaking vassalage, Moscow artificially fomented civil war, supporting and arming the internal opposition against the lawful hetman: "The proclamation of I. Vyhovsky as hetman was received negatively by the representatives of the forces opposed to him," led by Poltava colonel Pushkar and kish otaman Barabash(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 9 2012). Their revolt opened the period of the bloody Ruin.

Their revolt opened the period of the bloody Ruin.

objects.description: When covert methods of destabilization proved insufficient, the tsardom moved to open military invasion. The regular Muscovite army tried to subdue the Hetmanate by force, which ended in catastrophe at Konotop. The imperial historian Soloviev admitted: "The flower of the Muscovite cavalry, which had made the fortunate campaigns of '54 and '55, perished in a single day… Never again was the tsar of Muscovy able to field such a strong host"(Citation: История России с древнейших времён 1879).

objects.description: Taking advantage of the political crisis and having surrounded the autonomy's leaders with its troops, the tsardom forced them to sign a new, utterly enslaving treaty. The articles turned the confederative bond with Moscow into a federative one: "the Pereiaslav Articles converted Ukraine's confederative ties with Russia into the form of a federation. The Ukrainian state lost its independence and acquired the status of a political autonomy within the Russian state"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011). The very basis of the treaty was forged: "Prince Trubetskoy took advantage of his military superiority over Yu. Khmelnytsky, rejected the Zherdiv Articles and forced the Ukrainian side to accept 14 points of the so-called old articles of 1654 (which in reality constituted a falsification of the 1654 treaty)"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011). The 14 imposed points themselves are published in the "Collection of State Charters and Treaties"(Citation: Собрание государственных грамот и договоров. Часть 4 1828).

objects.description: The official partition of Ukrainian lands between two neighboring states. The treaty was signed exclusively by representatives of Moscow and Warsaw: "Concluded on January 30 (February 9) in the village of Andrusovo, near Smolensk, for 13.5 years. The Russian delegation was headed by okolnichy A. L. Ordin-Nashchokin, the Polish one by commissioner Yu. Hlebowicz"(Citation: Андрусовское перемирие 1667 2005). The opinion of the autonomy itself was completely ignored: "The interests of the hetmans and of Ukraine were, of course, not taken into account"(Citation: Мазепа 2007). A separate knot of the collusion was Kyiv: article 7 of the Andrusovo treaty (30 January 1667) stipulated that "the very city of Kyiv… is to be handed over and vacated… that is, within two years, counting from the present treaty… in the coming year 1669, on the 15th day of April"(Citation: Полное собрание законов Российской империи. Т. I 1830); "Muscovy then did not give it back"(Citation: Ілюстрована історія України 1921) - and in 1686 it legalized what it had withheld, "paying for Kyiv once more" (see the "Eternal Peace" campaign). The "territory for money" scheme was laid down in the same document: article 34 records Tsar Aleksei's consent to grant "a worthy treasury for the satisfaction of the szlachta exiles… from the part of Ukraine ceded to His Tsarist Majesty's side"(Citation: Полное собрание законов Российской империи. Т. I 1830) - with the sum deferred to future embassies.

objects.description: The deliberate dissolution of a distinct Ukrainian identity in the construct of a "single Orthodox people": the "Synopsis" subordinated Kyiv's history to the idea of a common "Slaveno-Rossian people"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 9 2012), and its political program presupposed a struggle for the "liberation… of the remaining part of the 'single Orthodox people'"(Citation: Украинский вопрос в политике властей и русском общественном мнении 2000). Hrushevsky points out what exactly was erased: the "Synopsis" is "a brief history of Rus composed at the Pechersk Lavra, done very lifelessly and incompletely (the history of the Cossacks, the struggle against Poland, and all of Ukraine's recent history are almost entirely omitted from it)"(Citation: Ілюстрована історія України 1921).

objects.description: The systematic dismantling of the autonomy's democratic institutions. Moscow categorically forbade the Cossacks to elect their leaders independently and to conduct an independent foreign policy: "and without a petition and without a decree of the great sovereigns... a hetman shall not be elected... nor shall they, on their own... write anything to anyone"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011). The abolition of the historical right to grant asylum: the autonomy was forced to perform the functions of the Muscovite punitive apparatus and to hand over fugitives: "and those fugitives and people of all ranks shall not be received, nor kept among them"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011).

objects.description: The division of spheres of influence behind the Ukrainian ally's back, accompanied by a financial deal for territory: under the 1686 treaty Moscow undertook "to count out one hundred forty-six thousand Muscovite rubles and hand them over to the Commonwealth"(Citation: Сборник грамот и договоров о присоединении царств и областей 1922)(Citation: Мазепа 2007)(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011). Ukrainian historiography recorded the deal as an ordinary purchase - Hrushevsky: Muscovy "concluded an eternal accord with Poland (paying, in addition, another 146 thousand rubles for Kyiv)"(Citation: Ілюстрована історія України 1921).

objects.description: The diplomatic entrenchment of spiritual expansion: Moscow secured the inclusion in the treaty of an article on the position of the Orthodox in the Commonwealth – the 1686 treaty ordered the Polish side "to inflict no oppression and no coercion toward the Roman faith or the Union"(Citation: Сборник грамот и договоров о присоединении царств и областей 1922) – and arrogated to itself the role of protector of Orthodoxy on Polish lands, relying on the Kyiv metropolitanate already subordinated to Moscow. The treaty also secured an ecclesiastical lever: the Orthodox eparchies in the Commonwealth "according to their spiritual rank and custom, are to receive blessing and ordination from the Metropolitan of Kyiv; and this shall harm none of them in the favor of His Royal Majesty"(Citation: Договор о Вечном мире с Польшей 1686) - while the Kyiv metropolitanate was already subordinated to Moscow.

objects.description: A course toward the complete absorption and destruction of the very name of the Cossack state. In the Bendery Constitution of 1710, Orlyk recorded Moscow's intention "to eradicate the Zaporozhian Host of the Lower Dnipro and to efface its name forever"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011). Hrushevsky confirms the course was systemic: Mazepa's alliance with the Swedish king merely "gave the Muscovite government occasion… to take up more forcefully the abolition of Ukrainian autonomy. The Muscovite government had pursued this line from the very beginning"(Citation: Ілюстрована історія України 1921). What was at stake was the enslavement of the entire people: the Muscovite state, per the preamble of Orlyk's constitution, managed to "violate and utterly destroy" the rights and liberties "and to cast a slave's yoke upon the free Cossack people, never conquered by it"(Citation: Договори і постанови прав і свобод військових (Конституція Пилипа Орлика) 1710).

objects.description: The anathema against Mazepa was proclaimed by the tsar's direct order - "be pleased to have him, for such a deed of his, publicly cursed in the cathedral church..."(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011). Part of the Ukrainian clergy refused to accept the rite: a former Lokhvytsia archpriest said during the proclamation of the anathema, "Our Mazepa is holy and will be in heaven, and your sovereign will not"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011). The Ecumenical Patriarchate never recognized it: "the anathema was laid on Ivan Mazepa for political reasons and had no theological or canonical justification"(Citation: Російська анафема Мазепи є неканонічною 2018).

objects.description: The installation of a government fully controlled by Moscow after the destruction of the capital: the election of the new hetman took place in Peter's presence immediately after the execution of the Baturyn officers – "Under the circumstances, the officers simply confirmed Skoropadsky, presented by Peter"(Citation: Мазепа 2007). Hrushevsky records the mechanics of dependence: "The hetman's residence was moved from Baturyn to Hlukhiv, right up against the Muscovite border, and two Muscovite regiments were garrisoned there so that the residents could arrest the hetman and the officers at once," and "everyone in Ukraine understood that power lay not with the hetman but with those residents"(Citation: Ілюстрована історія України 1921).

objects.description: The destruction of the political leadership that supported the hetman: "the entire (!) general starshyna" followed Mazepa, and of the Left-Bank colonels only four remained loyal to the tsar(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011). The investigation of the officers was directed from the tsar's headquarters, where "being at Lebedyn and Sumy, Peter and Menshikov in January 1709" oversaw the reprisals(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011). The ecclesiastical punishment was arranged by the tsar's direct order - by a letter of 31 October 1708 (No. 2795) Peter I instructed metropolitan Stefan Yavorsky: "be pleased to have him, for such a deed of his, publicly cursed in the cathedral church..."(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011)(Citation: Письма и бумаги императора Петра Великого. Т. VIII, вып. 1 (июль-декабрь 1708 г.) 1948).

objects.description: Intimidation of the population by an exemplary reprisal against an entire town: during the capture of Baturyn "in the bloody massacre and fire a multitude of the town's defenders and inhabitants perished"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011), "the town was razed to the ground and its inhabitants annihilated," and the returning residents were charged a special tax "for treason"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003). The devastation of the hetman capital also destroyed the state archive of the Hetmanate, which suffered "during the storming of Baturyn castle by A. Menshikov in 1708"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003).

objects.description: A punitive expedition against the Sich to physically annihilate the Lower Dnipro Cossacks: "Three infantry regiments led by Colonel P. Yakovlev were sent there. Keleberda was the first to be taken and burned on April 16. A stubborn battle was fought for Perevolochna"(Citation: Мазепа 2007). The assault on the Sich itself lasted four days. The punitive force was guided by mercenary colonel Hnat Galagan: in "1709 he took part in the destruction of the Zaporozhian Sich, for which he received four villages on the Right Bank"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004).

The punitive force was guided by mercenary colonel Hnat Galagan: in "1709 he took part in the destruction of the Zaporozhian Sich, for which he received four villages on the Right Bank"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004).

objects.description: The use of the church as an instrument of punishment: the anathema was proclaimed by the tsar's direct order - "be pleased to have him, for such a deed of his, publicly cursed in the cathedral church..."(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011). No theological grounding was supplied for it, and part of the Ukrainian clergy refused to accept the rite: a former Lokhvytsia archpriest said during the proclamation of the anathema, "Our Mazepa is holy and will be in heaven, and your sovereign will not"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011).

objects.description: The mass mobilization of Cossack regiments for penal construction labor: the digging of the Ladoga Canal "was carried out chiefly by the hands of Ukrainian Cossacks," and there "tens of thousands of people perished from back-breaking labor, hunger and the harsh climate"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 6 2009). In 1721 a "10,000-strong Cossack corps" headed by P. Polubotok was dispatched to the canal(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011); the works continued through 1721–23(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 9 2012).

objects.description: Shifting the upkeep of the mobilized onto the subjects themselves: Cossacks dispatched to the imperial construction sites were left without supply and "suffer great want from hunger, having neither food for themselves, nor winter quarters, nor fodder for the horses"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011). Workers for state construction the tsar simply ordered to be "taken from Ukraine, from those towns that are under your authority"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011), while at the works themselves people perished "from back-breaking labor, hunger and the harsh climate"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 6 2009).

История «предательства» 2011), while at the works themselves people perished "from back-breaking labor, hunger and the harsh climate"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 6 2009).

objects.description: The arrest of the acting hetman and officers in St. Petersburg for petitions defending autonomous rights. Peter was preparing a demonstrative reprisal: "Peter I planned to hold a show trial of Polubotok and his associates, accuse them of 'high treason,' and liquidate the Ukrainian autonomy. A special General Court was created for this purpose"(Citation: Смерть П. Полуботка в Петербурзі 2015). Only the prisoner's death derailed the plan: the hetman "died on December 21, 1724 (O.S.) of pneumonia"(Citation: Смерть П. Полуботка в Петербурзі 2015).

objects.description: The backroom partition of Ukraine along the Dnipro: by the "Eternal Peace" of 1686 Moscow officially ceded the Right Bank to Warsaw, without the participation or consent of Ukrainians themselves. The fate of the Right-Bank Cossacks was decided by foreign capitals: the ban of 1699 implemented this partition, against which Palii's Cossacks, "contrary to the terms of the 'Eternal Peace' of 1686," continued the struggle to unite both banks(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011).

objects.description: The collapse of the anti-Moscow coalition from within: on the Right Bank, the Tatar allies betrayed the Cossacks and turned to seizing the civilian population – "the Tatars, disobeying Orlyk, scattered in raiding parties and began taking yasyr captives across Ukrainian villages"(Citation: Мазепинці 1885). Orlyk himself wrote to the Swedish king: "What atrocities unheard of under the moon did the wild Tatars then commit!"(Citation: Мазепинці 1885).

objects.description: The final elimination of the office of the autonomy's leader: after Rozumovsky's forced abdication, Catherine II's decree of November 10, 1764 handed power to the Little Russian Collegium, whose president was instructed to act "with a governor's authority, that is, as our special plenipotentiary"(Citation: Указ об учреждении Малороссийской коллегии 1764). Catherine II's instruction to procurator-general Vyazemsky (1764) stated the goal openly: "and when there is no hetman in Little Russia, one must strive that the very age and name of hetmans vanish"(Citation: Наставление Екатерины II князю Вяземскому 1764).

objects.description: The use of Ukrainian Cossack regiments in the imperial war against the Ottoman Empire. The merits of the Zaporozhians and their kish otaman Kalnyshevsky in this war "were recognized by the tsarist government and the empress, who awarded him a gold medal with diamonds"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 4 2007) – which saved neither him nor the Sich from reprisal right after the victory.

objects.description: The signing of the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca: the diplomatic severing of Crimea from the Ottoman Empire through fictitious "independence" – "neither the Russian court nor the Ottoman Porte shall interfere in the election and elevation of the said khan, nor in their domestic, political, civil, and internal affairs under any pretext"(Citation: Кючук-Кайнарджийский мирный договор 1774) – in preparation for the subsequent annexation.

external_references.description: Кючук-Кайнарджийский мирный договор. 1774. – трактат Российской и Османской империй.

objects.description: The encirclement and forcible seizure of the Sich by imperial troops right after the Cossacks had helped the empire win the war. The manifesto records the operation matter-of-factly: "On June 4, Our Lieutenant-General Tekeli, with the troops entrusted to him by us, occupied the Zaporozhian Sich"(Citation: Манифест об уничтожении Запорожской Сечи 1775).

external_references.description: Екатерина II. Манифест об уничтожении Запорожской Сечи. 1775. – ПСЗРИ, т. XX, № 14354.

objects.description: The issuing of Catherine II's August manifesto, officially erasing the very memory of the Sich: it was destroyed "with the extirpation for the future of the very name of the Zaporozhian Cossacks," for the empire resolved "to destroy the Zaporozhian Sich and the name of the Cossacks derived from it"(Citation: Манифест об уничтожении Запорожской Сечи 1775). Hrushevsky: "The Sich was destroyed, and on 3 August a tsarist decree announced its abolition, 'with the annihilation of the very name of the Zaporozhian Cossacks'"(Citation: Ілюстрована історія України 1921).

external_references.description: Екатерина II. Манифест об уничтожении Запорожской Сечи. 1775. – ПСЗРИ, т. XX, № 14354.
Грушевський М. С. Ілюстрована історія України. 1921. – вид. з доведенням до 1918 р.; репринт Нью-Йорк, 1967.

objects.description: The arrest and exile of the Sich's top leadership: "In July 1775, after the destruction of the New Sich, by order of Empress Catherine II, Kalnyshevsky was arrested and sent to the prison of the Solovetsky monastery"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 4 2007). Kalnyshevsky spent more than 25 years in confinement; formally freed in 1801, he died in the monastery.

objects.description: The abolition of the Cossack regimental order and the division of the Left Bank into imperial viceroyalties: the Kyiv Viceroyalty was established by the nominal decree to the Senate of September 16, 1781 (PSZRI, coll. 1, vol. XXI, no. 15,228; execution ordered from November)(Citation: Именный указ, данный Сенату, об учреждении Киевского наместничества 1781)(Citation: Полное собрание законов Российской империи. Собрание первое. Том XXI (1781-1783) 1830), "which finally abolished the remnants of the Hetmanate's autonomy and its regimental-sotnia administrative-political and military order"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 4 2007); the same decree established the Chernihiv and Novhorod-Siverskyi viceroyalties.

objects.description: The secularization and confiscation into the imperial treasury of the lands of Ukrainian Orthodox monasteries: "in 1786, during the secularization, the monastery was closed, and its property and lands passed to the state treasury"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 9 2012) – the fate of the Sviatohirsk monastery is typical of the entire 1786 campaign, which deprived the local church of its economic base.

objects.description: The colonization of the steppes adjacent to Crimea with settlers to create a loyal rear: as early as 1752, New Serbia was formed from Serbs – "officially – to guard the southern frontiers from Tatar and Turkish raids, but in fact – to subdue the Zaporozhians"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 9 2012), and in 1776 Potemkin directly ordered "not to return fugitives"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011), accelerating the settlement of the south.

objects.description: In 1804-1811 the Russian Empire put up a cast-iron Monument of Glory in the center of Poltava in memory of its victory over the army of Charles XII on 27 June 1709 - with the city's own money and to a design sent from St. Petersburg. By the imperial decree to the Senate of 11 September 1804, "On leaving the villages formerly owned by the city of Poltava under state administration and on releasing the income collected from them to the local Governor-General for the construction in Poltava of a monument in memory of 27 June 1709," the city's revenues were assigned to the monument: "the community of Poltava citizens, through a petition submitted to Governor-General Prince Kurakin, has designated all these revenues for the construction in Poltava of a monument in memory of the day unforgettable for Russia, 27 June 1709, and so we command: the revenues now due for payment, as well as those henceforth collected in favor of this city, shall be released to the local Governor-General until the monument that has been begun is completely finished"(Citation: Полное собрание законов Российской империи, Собрание 1-е, том XXVIII (1804-1805) 1830). By a second act, the imperial rescript of 9 May 1805 to the Governor-General of Little Russia, "On the construction of a monument in commemoration of the victory won at Poltava by Emperor Peter the Great," the emperor sent a ready-made design and ordered construction to begin: "I forward to you herewith the plans for this monument, drawn up here, charging you... to proceed with its construction on site, except for the bronze ornaments belonging to it, which will be made separately here and delivered to their destination"(Citation: Полное собрание законов Российской империи, Собрание 1-е, том XXVIII (1804-1805) 1830). That is, Poltava pays, while Petersburg decides what the sign on its land will look like - down to the bronze, which is cast there and shipped ready-made. The monument was founded on 27 June 1804, the cast-iron column was raised in May 1809 under the direction of Moskvin, an engineer of the Luhansk works, and the whole ensemble was opened on 27 June 1811, for the next anniversary of the battle(Citation: Записки о Полтаве и её памятниках 1902)(Citation: Паспорт пам'ятки. Монумент Слави [1990 р.] 1990). On the medallion of the upper square of the pedestal, inside a serpent ring between two quivers, stood "June the 27th, 1709," and on the opposite side - "Finished in 1809"(Citation: Записки о Полтаве и её памятниках 1902): the date of someone else's victory was made into the date of the place itself. Both inscriptions, together with the bronze bas-reliefs, disappeared in 1901 - the pre-revolutionary survey records it tersely: "This inscription and the preceding one were destroyed in 1901, and at the same time the bronze bas-reliefs that surrounded them were taken by persons unknown"(Citation: Записки о Полтаве и её памятниках 1902); they were restored only during the capital repairs of 1953(Citation: Паспорт пам'ятки. Монумент Слави [1990 р.] 1990). The monument still stands in Poltava: as of August 2026 it is listed as a monument of national significance under heritage protection number 160010-Н(Citation: Перелік об'єктів культурної спадщини Полтавської міської територіальної громади (категорія «Національного значення») 2025), the Ukrainian Institute of National Remembrance recommended dismantling it in a letter of 29 July 2024(Citation: Лист УІНП №2075/2.2-08-24 щодо Монумента Слави у м. Полтава 2024), but decisions on monuments of national significance are made by the government, and the list of such decisions as of 20 May 2026 does not include the monument(Citation: Рішення Мінкульту щодо переміщення чи зняття статусу пам'яток в рамках декомунізації, дерусифікації та деколонізації (станом на 20.05.2026) 2026).

objects.description: In 1804-1811 the Russian Empire put up a cast-iron Monument of Glory in the center of Poltava in memory of its victory over the army of Charles XII on 27 June 1709 - with the city's own money and to a design sent from St. Petersburg. By the imperial decree to the Senate of 11 September 1804, "On leaving the villages formerly owned by the city of Poltava under state administration and on releasing the income collected from them to the local Governor-General for the construction in Poltava of a monument in memory of 27 June 1709," the city's revenues were assigned to the monument: "the community of Poltava citizens, through a petition submitted to Governor-General Prince Kurakin, has designated all these revenues for the construction in Poltava of a monument in memory of the day unforgettable for Russia, 27 June 1709, and so we command: the revenues now due for payment, as well as those henceforth collected in favor of this city, shall be released to the local Governor-General until the monument that has been begun is completely finished"(Citation: Полное собрание законов Российской империи, Собрание 1-е, том XXVIII (1804-1805) 1830). By a second act, the imperial rescript of 9 May 1805 to the Governor-General of Little Russia, "On the construction of a monument in commemoration of the victory won at Poltava by Emperor Peter the Great," the emperor sent a ready-made design and ordered construction to begin: "I forward to you herewith the plans for this monument, drawn up here, charging you... to proceed with its construction on site, except for the bronze ornaments belonging to it, which will be made separately here and delivered to their destination"(Citation: Полное собрание законов Российской империи, Собрание 1-е, том XXVIII (1804-1805) 1830). That is, Poltava pays, while Petersburg decides what the sign on its land will look like - down to the bronze, which is cast there and shipped ready-made. The monument was founded on 27 June 1804, the cast-iron column was raised in May 1809 under the direction of Moskvin, an engineer of the Luhansk works, and the whole ensemble was opened on 27 June 1811, for the next anniversary of the battle(Citation: Записки о Полтаве и её памятниках 1902)(Citation: Паспорт пам'ятки. Монумент Слави [1990 р.] 1990). On the medallion of the upper square of the pedestal, inside a serpent ring between two quivers, stood "June the 27th, 1709," and on the opposite side - "Finished in 1809"(Citation: Записки о Полтаве и её памятниках 1902): the date of someone else's victory was made into the date of the place itself. Both inscriptions, together with the bronze bas-reliefs, disappeared in 1901 - the pre-revolutionary survey records it tersely: "This inscription and the preceding one were destroyed in 1901, and at the same time the bronze bas-reliefs that surrounded them were taken by persons unknown"(Citation: Записки о Полтаве и её памятниках 1902); they were restored only during the capital repairs of 1953(Citation: Паспорт пам'ятки. Монумент Слави [1990 р.] 1990). The monument still stands in Poltava: as of August 2026 it is listed as a monument of national significance under heritage protection number 160010-Н(Citation: Перелік об'єктів культурної спадщини Полтавської міської територіальної громади (категорія «Національного значення») 2025), the Ukrainian Institute of National Remembrance recommended dismantling it in a letter of 29 July 2024(Citation: Лист УІНП №2075/2.2-08-24 щодо Монумента Слави у м. Полтава 2024), but decisions on monuments of national significance are made by the government, and the list of such decisions as of 20 May 2026 does not include the monument(Citation: Рішення Мінкульту щодо переміщення чи зняття статусу пам'яток в рамках декомунізації, дерусифікації та деколонізації (станом на 20.05.2026) 2026).

objects.description: The transfer of Cossacks to the status of rightless military settlers (the Arakcheev system), which provoked the uprising of 1817: "The trigger was the order abolishing the Buh Cossack Host and turning the Cossacks into military settlers… The reprisal against the rebellious Cossacks was extraordinarily brutal: many were cut down with sabers, drowned in the Southern Buh, flogged to death"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003). There were two acts, on opposite sides of the uprising: the nominal decree of April 17, 1817 transferred the Buh Host's district "into direct military administration" (PSZRI, vol. XXXIV, no. 26,802) - this was the trigger; the decree of October 8, 1817 (no. 27,081), issued after the suppression, formalized the liquidation: "the name of the Buh Cossack Host is abolished"(Citation: Полное собрание законов Российской империи. Собрание первое. Том XXXIV (1817) 1830).

external_references.description: Інститут історії України НАН України. Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1. 2003. – редкол.: Смолій В. А. (голова) та ін.

objects.description: The Russification of teaching in the country's principal institution of learning: from 1784 metropolitan Samuil Myslavsky introduced new classes of geography and history at the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy with an order to conduct them "in pure Russian," and by his order of 26 October 1784 demanded that teachers and students observe "the rules of orthography proper to the Russian language" - teachers faced dismissal for lapses, and students expulsion from the clerical estate(Citation: Українська церква: Нариси з історії української православної церкви (гл. XIII. Як цариця Катерина обмосковлювала Церкву Українську) 1993). The unification was completed by the order of February 13, 1786: "to adopt immediately for the Kyiv Academy the mode of instruction legalized for all schools in the All-Russian Empire"(Citation: Навічно кували кайдани 1995) – the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy was transferred to the empire-wide mode of teaching.

external_references.source_name: Українська церква: Нариси з історії української православної церкви (гл. XIII. Як цариця Катерина обмосковлювала Церкву Українську) 1993
external_references.description: Огієнко І. (митрополит Іларіон). Українська церква: Нариси з історії української православної церкви (гл. XIII. Як цариця Катерина обмосковлювала Церкву Українську). 1993.
Лизанчук В. В. Навічно кували кайдани. 1995.

objects.description: The displacement of the local population's language from the sacred sphere: metropolitan Samuil Myslavsky's order of 26 October 1784 demanded that students and future priests practice "the reading of church books of every kind, and above all the Bible, acquiring a good and pure pronunciation" - after the Moscow model instead of the Ukrainian church tradition, under the threat of expulsion from the clerical estate(Citation: Українська церква: Нариси з історії української православної церкви (гл. objects.description: A concession that was in fact a choice between two alien orthographies: the 1881 revision allowed dictionaries to be printed, but "on condition of their being printed in conformity with all-Russian orthography, or with the orthography used in Little Russia no later than the 18th century"(Citation: Українська ідентичність і мовне питання в Російській імперії 2013). That is, either the metropole's orthography or an archaic one was admissible - contemporary Ukrainian orthography was not allowed in any form. The same document permitted stage texts to musical scores to be printed only "on condition of generally accepted Russian orthography," and made Ukrainian-language performances dependent on administrative permission: "dramatic plays, scenes and couplets in the Little Russian dialect... may be performed on stage, each time, however, with the special permission of the governors-general, and in localities not subordinate to governors-general - with the permission of the governors"(Citation: Українська ідентичність і мовне питання в Російській імперії 2013).

objects.description: The theater was banned not as repertoire but as an institution: the third point of the 1881 revision prescribed "to completely forbid the establishment of a specifically Little Russian theater and the formation of troupes for performing plays and scenes exclusively in the Little Russian dialect"(Citation: Українська ідентичність і мовне питання в Російській імперії 2013). Individual plays remained permissible - with administrative permission for each staging. The ban struck not at the text but at the very possibility of a permanent company existing: performing occasionally was allowed, being a Ukrainian theater was not. objects.description: The ban on the language in public speech: at the archaeological congress in Kyiv in 1899 the authorities forbade scholars from Austrian-ruled Ukraine to read papers in Ukrainian - they demonstratively withdrew from the sessions(Citation: Українська мова в першій половині двадцятого століття (1900-1941). Стан і статус 1987). At the unveiling of the Kotliarevsky monument in Poltava on 30-31 August 1903, the Galicians were allowed to speak Ukrainian, but when local Ukrainians began reading a greeting address, the mayor cut the reading short, citing an order of the ministry of internal affairs; only in 1906 did the Senate revoke the ban, even reprimanding the minister for "the impropriety of his actions"(Citation: Українська мова в першій половині двадцятого століття (1900-1941). Стан і статус 1987). In 1904-1905 the commissions of the Kyiv and Kharkiv universities and the Academy of Sciences, consulted by the Committee of Ministers, spoke out for lifting the bans on the Ukrainian word, yet the decrees of 1876 and 1881 were never formally revoked(Citation: Українська мова в першій половині двадцятого століття (1900-1941). Стан і статус 1987).

The censor's resolution on a children's collection: "Obviously written for children, but they must learn in Russian. — Forbid"(Citation: Навічно кували кайдани 1995).

objects.description:
The direct closure of legal educational societies: of the roughly forty "Prosvitas" of Russian-ruled Ukraine, those in the Poltava and Kharkiv regions were banned from their very founding, and in 1908–1910, under Stolypin, virtually all the rest were liquidated, except the branches of the Katerynoslav governorate(Citation: Українська мова в першій половині двадцятого століття (1900-1941). Стан і статус 1987). The crackdown received its doctrinal grounding: Stolypin declared in an address to the Senate that the revival of Ukrainian cultural life was undesirable, for "the three principal branches of Eastern Slavdom, both by origin and by language, cannot but constitute one whole"(Citation: Українська мова в першій половині двадцятого століття (1900-1941). Стан і статус 1987).
Stolypin's circular to the governors (20 January 1910) — a complete ban on self-organization: "when considering petitions for the registration of any alien societies whatsoever… one must… refuse without fail the registration of their charters"(Citation: Столыпинский циркуляр 1910).

objects.description: The purge of the information space: Nicholas II's personal decree of 20 July 1914 on military censorship gave the command the right "to forbid for a set term, by their own authority and within the locality subordinate to them, any assemblies whatsoever, and to suspend periodical publications, as well as the transmission of postal items and telegrams"(Citation: Указ об утверждении временного Положения о военной цензуре 1914). On this basis the military administration of the Kyiv military district that very day closed the only Ukrainian daily newspaper, "Rada," and confiscated at the printing house the print runs of "Svitlo" and of the "Literary-Scientific Herald," and on 9 January 1915 all Ukrainian periodicals were shut down(Citation: Українська мова в першій половині двадцятого століття (1900-1941). Стан і статус 1987).

objects.description: The targeted physical annihilation of the national cultural elite. The official turn was sealed by the resolution of the Central Committee of the VKP(b) and the Council of People's Commissars "On Grain Procurements in Ukraine, the North Caucasus, and the Western Region" of 14 December 1932, signed by Stalin and Molotov: Ukrainization was declared to have been carried out "mechanically," which, in the resolution's own words, "made it easier for bourgeois-nationalist elements, Petliurites and the like to create their legal covers, their counter-revolutionary cells and organizations"(Citation: О хлебозаготовках на Украине, Северном Кавказе и в Западной области 1932). The term "Executed Renaissance" denotes precisely "the repressive policy of communist Moscow aimed at the physical destruction of the Ukrainian intellectual elite of the 1920s–30s (more broadly – of the entire nationally conscious Ukrainian intelligentsia) and the tabooing of its creative achievements"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 9 2012).

Інститут історії України НАН України. Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 9. 2012. – редкол.: Смолій В. А. (голова) та ін.

objects.description: The material sign of the "merging of nations" was put up in Pereiaslav in the Kyiv region, the city of the Pereiaslav Rada: "on 8 October 1961, a majestic monument in honor of the 300th anniversary of the reunification of Ukraine with Russia was unveiled on B. Khmelnytsky Square"(Citation: Історія міст і сіл Української РСР. Київська область 1971). The authorities unveiled the sign themselves: according to the newsreel Radianska Ukraina No. 49, the opening rally was addressed by Petro Shelest, first secretary of the Kyiv obkom of the CPU, and Pankratov, a secretary of the Moscow obkom of the party - the metropole spoke at the unveiling in its own voice(Citation: Радянська Україна. Кіножурнал № 49 1961). The composition consisted of two female figures representing Ukraine and Russia and three bas-reliefs with medallions: "a torch, 1654; a hammer and sickle in the rays of the sun, 1917; the Order of Victory, 1945"(Citation: Куди подінуть пам'ятник «возз'єднання» у Переяславі 2022). The sign's purpose is recorded in its own protection passport: "The monument is a symbol of the eternal, unbreakable friendship and the indestructible monolithic unity of the fraternal peoples - Ukrainian and Russian…"(Citation: Геть від Москви чи навіки разом? Що робити з пам'ятниками, які виконують роль ідеологічної отрути 2020). Four years after the unveiling, the sign was taken under state protection by the resolution of the Council of Ministers of the Ukrainian SSR of 21 July 1965 No. 711 "On the approval of the list of monuments of art, history and archaeology of the Ukrainian SSR"(Citation: Про затвердження списку пам'яток мистецтва, історії та археології Української РСР 1965)(Citation: Наказ Міністерства культури і туризму України № 58/0/16-10 2010). The pedestal bore the inscription "Forever together - forever with the Russian people"; in early December 2021 it was removed by unknown persons(Citation: У столиці демонтують скульптуру-символ возз'єднання України з росією. А що в Переяславі? 2022), and the monument itself was dismantled on 7 July 2022 - by an order of the Ministry of Culture that struck the monument, protection No. 5894-Ko, off the register "due to the loss of the subject of protection"(Citation: Наказ Міністерства культури та інформаційної політики України № 223 2022).

objects.description: The material sign of the "merging of nations" was put up in Pereiaslav in the Kyiv region, the city of the Pereiaslav Rada: "on 8 October 1961, a majestic monument in honor of the 300th anniversary of the reunification of Ukraine with Russia was unveiled on B. Khmelnytsky Square"(Citation: Історія міст і сіл Української РСР. Київська область 1971). The authorities unveiled the sign themselves: according to the newsreel Radianska Ukraina No. 49, the opening rally was addressed by Petro Shelest, first secretary of the Kyiv obkom of the CPU, and Pankratov, a secretary of the Moscow obkom of the party - the metropole spoke at the unveiling in its own voice(Citation: Радянська Україна. Кіножурнал № 49 1961). The composition consisted of two female figures representing Ukraine and Russia and three bas-reliefs with medallions: "a torch, 1654; a hammer and sickle in the rays of the sun, 1917; the Order of Victory, 1945"(Citation: Куди подінуть пам'ятник «возз'єднання» у Переяславі 2022). The sign's purpose is recorded in its own protection passport: "The monument is a symbol of the eternal, unbreakable friendship and the indestructible monolithic unity of the fraternal peoples - Ukrainian and Russian…"(Citation: Геть від Москви чи навіки разом? Що робити з пам'ятниками, які виконують роль ідеологічної отрути 2020). Four years after the unveiling, the sign was taken under state protection by the resolution of the Council of Ministers of the Ukrainian SSR of 21 July 1965 No. 711 "On the approval of the list of monuments of art, history and archaeology of the Ukrainian SSR"(Citation: Про затвердження списку пам'яток мистецтва, історії та археології Української РСР 1965)(Citation: Наказ Міністерства культури і туризму України № 58/0/16-10 2010). The pedestal bore the inscription "Forever together - forever with the Russian people"; in early December 2021 it was removed by unknown persons(Citation: У столиці демонтують скульптуру-символ возз'єднання України з росією. А що в Переяславі? 2022), and the monument itself was dismantled on 7 July 2022 - by an order of the Ministry of Culture that struck the monument, protection No. 5894-Ko, off the register "due to the loss of the subject of protection"(Citation: Наказ Міністерства культури та інформаційної політики України № 223 2022).

objects.description: Arrests, interrogations – the gendarmes "resorted to brutal pressure" and "applied refined methods of psychological processing"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 4 2007), and reprisal against the leaders: the sentences were set out in the report of the chief of gendarmes Orlov to the emperor of May 26, 1847, with Nicholas I's resolution "Execute"(Citation: Кирило-Мефодіївське товариство: У 3 т. 1990). Shevchenko was sent into the army "with the institution over the poet of 'the strictest surveillance with a prohibition on writing and drawing'"(Citation: Труды и дни Кобзаря 1996)(Citation: Кирило-Мефодіївське товариство: У 3 т. 1990). Hrushevsky: the brotherhood "was seized while still in the midst of its very formation" after a student's denunciation; "The heaviest punishment fell on Shevchenko: he was given over to the soldiery and exiled to the trans-Caspian desert, forbidden to write and to paint," and "persecutions and prohibitions previously unheard of descended upon Ukrainian thought and the Ukrainian word… the very words Ukraine, Little Russia, Hetmanate were deemed criminal"(Citation: Ілюстрована історія України 1921). The brotherhood's co-founder Mykola Hulak "was imprisoned in the Shlisselburg fortress (1847-50), then exiled to Perm under strict police surveillance (1850-59)"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004).

objects.description: The systematic imposition of the metropole's logic of superiority. Researchers reconstruct Katkov's logic thus: "a nation must be a tribe capable of creating a state; only a state nation can establish order in a given territory; tribes incapable of creating a state have to submit to the state nation"(Citation: Политический национализм М. Н. Каткова 2018). Katkov himself wrote: "In the recognition of a nation the question of power, of government, of the state is decided"(Citation: Политический национализм М. Н. Каткова 2018). Hrushevsky records both the thesis and its reach: Valuev invoked an imaginary "majority of Little Russians" who allegedly "know neither a Ukrainian nationality nor language, only one Russian people and tongue," while the ideology's mouthpieces carried it to the formula "there are no Ruthenians — there is only one 'Russian people' from the Carpathians to Kamchatka"(Citation: Ілюстрована історія України 1921).

objects.description: On the pedestal of the Khmelnytsky monument (1888) the empire cast a programmatic statement about the past: on the front side stood the phrase "We will to be under the tsar of the east, the Orthodox one," attributed to the Pereiaslav Rada, and on the right - the imperial formula "To Bohdan Khmelnytsky – one and indivisible Russia"(Citation: Пам'ятник Богдану Хмельницькому в Києві 2026).
