objects.description:
On December 12, 1919, the command of the Soviet Southern Front issued secret directive No. 188. The document was signed by front commander Yegorov, the future head of the USSR Stalin, and chief of staff Petin. The directive gave the invaders' army its task: «to capture the city of Kyiv in the shortest possible time»(Citation: Директивы командования фронтов Красной армии (1917–1922). Т. 2 1972). On December 16, 1919, the army of Soviet Russia (RSFSR) took Kyiv for the third time since the start of the communist revolution(Citation: Директивы командования фронтов Красной армии (1917–1922). Т. 2 1972)(Citation: Відносини держави, суспільства і особи під час створення радянського ладу в Україні (1917 – 1938 рр.) 2013).
The Ukrainian People's Republic (UNR) is the Ukrainian state proclaimed in 1917. By December 1919 its army - eight to ten thousand soldiers, many of them sick with typhus - was pinned near Starokostiantyniv in Volhynia: the Volunteer Army of Denikin to the south and east, the Polish army to the west, the troops of Soviet Russia to the north. Contemporaries called this position the «triangle of death»(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011). At a meeting in Nova Chortoryia on December 4-6, 1919, the head of the UNR Directory Symon Petliura and the army command decided to dissolve the regular front. The UNR Army under the command of Mykhailo Omelianovych-Pavlenko set out on a raid through the rear of the Soviet and White forces: in 180 days, from December 6, 1919 to May 6, 1920, some ten thousand soldiers marched two and a half thousand kilometres across Ukraine. This raid is known as the First Winter Campaign(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011).
That same winter Soviet troops occupied most of Ukraine. The dates of the cities' capture, according to the front reports: December 11, 1919 - Poltava and Kharkiv, December 16 - Kupiansk, December 24 - Luhansk, January 5, 1920 - Mariupol, February 7 - Odesa(Citation: Директивы командования фронтов Красной армии (1917–1922). Т. 2 1972). On the Right Bank the Russian occupier reached the Polish front line: Kamianets-Podilskyi, Proskuriv and Starokostiantyniv were held by the Poles(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011).
The UNR leadership signed an alliance with Poland and secured the support of its army in the fight against the Russian occupiers. In the spring of 1920 the armies of Poland and the UNR moved to liberate Kyiv. On May 6, 1920, Yegorov, commander of the Southwestern Front of the Soviet army, telegraphed in secret order No. 304: «Kyiv must fall to the enemy only at the cost of the heaviest losses on his part»(Citation: Директивы командования фронтов Красной армии (1917–1922). Т. 3 1974). The armies of the UNR and Poland retook Kyiv: on May 7 Polish reconnaissance units rode to the centre of the city by tram, and on May 8 ten regiments of the 3rd Polish Army entered the capital(Citation: Нариси історії Української революції 1917–1921 років: Кн. 2 2012).
The occupier gathered its forces and on June 6 broke through the Polish front south of Kyiv, at Samhorodok. On June 10 the Polish troops, having blown up the Chain and Rusanivskyi bridges, withdrew from Kyiv(Citation: Нариси історії Української революції 1917–1921 років: Кн. 2 2012). On June 12, 1920, Yegorov reported: «Units of the 58th Division have taken Pechersk and are entering Kyiv». The orders to cut the Kyiv - Korosten railway, issued the day before, were signed by Yegorov and Stalin(Citation: Директивы командования фронтов Красной армии (1917–1922). Т. 3 1974).
On October 18, 1920, an armistice took effect on the Polish-Soviet front, and the UNR Army was left to face the invader alone(Citation: Нариси історії Української революції 1917–1921 років: Кн. 2 2012). By November 10 it held the front with 8,968 bayonets and 3,250 sabres, with 95 guns and 687 machine guns. Against it the Soviet command moved the 12th and 14th armies, the Bashkir cavalry brigade and Kotovsky's cavalry brigade: 24,000 bayonets, 4,000 sabres, 120 guns and five armoured trains(Citation: Останні дні збройної боротьби (21.XI.1920 — 21.XI.1930) 1930). The occupation troops attacked first and thwarted the offensive being prepared in Podillia, in today's Vinnytsia and Khmelnytskyi oblasts. In eleven days of fighting the UNR Army lost about 13 thousand soldiers, almost all of its artillery and four armoured trains(Citation: Нариси історії Української революції 1917–1921 років: Кн. 2 2012).
On November 21, 1920, about 12 thousand UNR soldiers, together with the staff of Symon Petliura and the ministries, crossed the Zbruch River, along which ran the border with the lands ceded to Poland under the Treaty of Warsaw(Citation: Нариси історії Української революції 1917–1921 років: Кн. 2 2012). Mykhailo Andrusiak, a participant in the retreat, recalled: «Sadly, with bowed heads, the Cossacks laid down their arms after crossing the bridge and marched on to the West»(Citation: Останній відступ (Спомини М. Андрусяка) 1930).
In the autumn of 1921 the soldiers of the UNR army made a last attempt to raise a general uprising against the Soviet occupiers. This raid is known as the Second Winter Campaign, and its course is known from the report of the chief of the Field Insurgent Staff, Colonel Yurii Otmarshtein, submitted to Symon Petliura. At 2 a.m. on November 4, 1921, the detachment crossed the Polish-Ukrainian border near the village of Borove: 155 officers and officials, 645 Cossacks, 32 horses, with about 56 percent of the men armed with rifles(Citation: До історії повстанчого рейду ген. хор. Ю. Тютюнника в листопаді 1921 р. (Доклад начальника Польового Повстанчого Штабу) 1930). On November 7 the detachment under the overall command of Yurii Tiutiunnyk liberated the Korosten railway junction in battle and freed 600 political prisoners from the jail, but withdrew that same morning: an armoured train of the Soviet occupiers was approaching the town with guns the detachment had nothing to counter, and ammunition had to be spared. Seven officers and twelve Cossacks died in the battle(Citation: До історії повстанчого рейду ген. хор. Ю. Тютюнника в листопаді 1921 р. (Доклад начальника Польового Повстанчого Штабу) 1930).
The detachment could go no further. Half of the infantry marched without boots and with frostbitten feet, the wagon train carried up to 80 wounded, and ammunition was replenished only with what was taken from killed and captured Russians. The staff decided to turn back, towards Poland(Citation: До історії повстанчого рейду ген. хор. Ю. Тютюнника в листопаді 1921 р. (Доклад начальника Польового Повстанчого Штабу) 1930). The troops of the Russian invader blockaded the area of the UNR raid and on November 17 encircled the detachment near the village of Mali Mynky in the north of Zhytomyr Oblast. Over 400 soldiers died in the battle, 537 were taken prisoner, and more than a hundred broke out of the encirclement and crossed the Polish border on November 20(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003)(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004). The prisoners were taken to the village of Bazar, where 359 of them were shot(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963). The armed struggle of the regular UNR Army ended there(Citation: Україна й українці в постімперську добу (1917—1939) 2021).

On November 21, 1920, about 12 thousand UNR soldiers, together with the staff of Symon Petliura and the ministries, crossed the Zbruch River, along which ran the border with the lands ceded to Poland under the Treaty of Warsaw(Citation: Нариси історії Української революції 1917–1921 років: Кн. 2 2012). Mykhailo Andrusiak, a participant in the retreat, recalled: «Sadly, with bowed heads, the Cossacks laid down their arms after crossing the bridge and marched on to the West»(Citation: Останній відступ (Спомини М. Андрусяка) 1930).
In the autumn of 1921 the soldiers of the UNR army made a last attempt to raise a general uprising against the Soviet occupiers. This raid is known as the Second Winter Campaign, and its course is known from the report of the chief of the Field Insurgent Staff, Colonel Yurii Otmarshtein, submitted to Symon Petliura. At 2 a.m. on November 4, 1921, the detachment crossed the Polish-Ukrainian border near the village of Borove: 155 officers and officials, 645 Cossacks, 32 horses, with about 56 percent of the men armed with rifles(Citation: До історії повстанчого рейду ген. хор. Ю. Тютюнника в листопаді 1921 р. (Доклад начальника Польового Повстанчого Штабу) 1930). On November 7 the detachment under the overall command of Yurii Tiutiunnyk liberated the Korosten railway junction in battle and freed 600 political prisoners from the jail, but withdrew that same morning: an armoured train of the Soviet occupiers was approaching the town with guns the detachment had nothing to counter, and ammunition had to be spared. Seven officers and twelve Cossacks died in the battle(Citation: До історії повстанчого рейду ген. хор. Ю. Тютюнника в листопаді 1921 р. (Доклад начальника Польового Повстанчого Штабу) 1930).
The detachment could go no further. Half of the infantry marched without boots and with frostbitten feet, the wagon train carried up to 80 wounded, and ammunition was replenished only with what was taken from killed and captured Russians. The staff decided to turn back, towards Poland(Citation: До історії повстанчого рейду ген. хор. Ю. Тютюнника в листопаді 1921 р. (Доклад начальника Польового Повстанчого Штабу) 1930). The troops of the Russian invader blockaded the area of the UNR raid and on November 17 encircled the detachment near the village of Mali Mynky in the north of Zhytomyr Oblast. Over 400 soldiers died in the battle, 537 were taken prisoner, and more than a hundred broke out of the encirclement and crossed the Polish border on November 20(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003)(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004). The prisoners were taken to the village of Bazar, where 359 of them were shot(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963). On December 12, 1919, the command of the Soviet Southern Front issued secret directive No. 188. The document was signed by front commander Yegorov, the future head of the USSR Stalin, and chief of staff Petin. The directive gave the invaders' army its task: «to capture the city of Kyiv in the shortest possible time»(Citation: Директивы командования фронтов Красной армии (1917–1922). Т. 2 1972). On December 16, 1919, the army of Soviet Russia (RSFSR) took Kyiv for the third time since the start of the communist revolution(Citation: Директивы командования фронтов Красной армии (1917–1922). Т. 2 1972)(Citation: Відносини держави, суспільства і особи під час створення радянського ладу в Україні (1917 – 1938 рр.) 2013).
The Ukrainian People's Republic (UNR) is the Ukrainian state proclaimed in 1917. By December 1919 its army - eight to ten thousand soldiers, many of them sick with typhus - was pinned near Starokostiantyniv in Volhynia: the Volunteer Army of Denikin to the south and east, the Polish army to the west, the troops of Soviet Russia to the north. Contemporaries called this position the «triangle of death»(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011). At a meeting in Nova Chortoryia on December 4-6, 1919, the head of the UNR Directory Symon Petliura and the army command decided to dissolve the regular front. The UNR Army under the command of Mykhailo Omelianovych-Pavlenko set out on a raid through the rear of the Soviet and White forces: in 180 days, from December 6, 1919 to May 6, 1920, some ten thousand soldiers marched two and a half thousand kilometres across Ukraine. This raid is known as the First Winter Campaign(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011).
That same winter Soviet troops occupied most of Ukraine. The dates of the cities' capture, according to the front reports: December 11, 1919 - Poltava and Kharkiv, December 16 - Kupiansk, December 24 - Luhansk, January 5, 1920 - Mariupol, February 7 - Odesa(Citation: Директивы командования фронтов Красной армии (1917–1922). Т. 2 1972). On the Right Bank the Russian occupier reached the Polish front line: Kamianets-Podilskyi, Proskuriv and Starokostiantyniv were held by the Poles(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011).
The UNR leadership signed an alliance with Poland and secured the support of its army in the fight against the Russian occupiers. In the spring of 1920 the armies of Poland and the UNR moved to liberate Kyiv. Т. 3 1974). The armies of the UNR and Poland retook Kyiv: on May 7 Polish reconnaissance units rode to the centre of the city by tram, and on May 8 ten regiments of the 3rd Polish Army entered the capital(Citation: Нариси історії Української революції 1917–1921 років: Кн. 2 2012).
The occupier gathered its forces and on June 6 broke through the Polish front south of Kyiv, at Samhorodok. On June 10 the Polish troops, having blown up the Chain and Rusanivskyi bridges, withdrew from Kyiv(Citation: Нариси історії Української революції 1917–1921 років: Кн. 2 2012). On June 12, 1920, Yegorov reported: «Units of the 58th Division have taken Pechersk and are entering Kyiv». objects.description:
On December 12, 1919, the command of the Soviet Southern Front issued secret directive No. 188. The document was signed by front commander Yegorov, the future head of the USSR Stalin, and chief of staff Petin. The directive gave the invaders' army its task: «to capture the city of Kyiv in the shortest possible time»(Citation: Директивы командования фронтов Красной армии (1917–1922). Т. 2 1972). On December 16, 1919, the army of Soviet Russia (RSFSR) took Kyiv for the third time since the start of the communist revolution(Citation: Директивы командования фронтов Красной армии (1917–1922). Т. 2 1972)(Citation: Відносини держави, суспільства і особи під час створення радянського ладу в Україні (1917 – 1938 рр.) 2013).
The Ukrainian People's Republic (UNR) is the Ukrainian state proclaimed in 1917. By December 1919 its army - eight to ten thousand soldiers, many of them sick with typhus - was pinned near Starokostiantyniv in Volhynia: the Volunteer Army of Denikin to the south and east, the Polish army to the west, the troops of Soviet Russia to the north. Contemporaries called this position the «triangle of death»(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011). At a meeting in Nova Chortoryia on December 4-6, 1919, the head of the UNR Directory Symon Petliura and the army command decided to dissolve the regular front. The UNR Army under the command of Mykhailo Omelianovych-Pavlenko set out on a raid through the rear of the Soviet and White forces: in 180 days, from December 6, 1919 to May 6, 1920, some ten thousand soldiers marched two and a half thousand kilometres across Ukraine. This raid is known as the First Winter Campaign(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011).
That same winter Soviet troops occupied most of Ukraine. The dates of the cities' capture, according to the front reports: December 11, 1919 - Poltava and Kharkiv, December 16 - Kupiansk, December 24 - Luhansk, January 5, 1920 - Mariupol, February 7 - Odesa(Citation: Директивы командования фронтов Красной армии (1917–1922). Т. 2 1972). On the Right Bank the Russian occupier reached the Polish front line: Kamianets-Podilskyi, Proskuriv and Starokostiantyniv were held by the Poles(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011).
The UNR leadership signed an alliance with Poland and secured the support of its army in the fight against the Russian occupiers. In the spring of 1920 the armies of Poland and the UNR moved to liberate Kyiv. On May 6, 1920, Yegorov, commander of the Southwestern Front of the Soviet army, telegraphed in secret order No. 304: «Kyiv must fall to the enemy only at the cost of the heaviest losses on his part»(Citation: Директивы командования фронтов Красной армии (1917–1922). Т. 3 1974). The armies of the UNR and Poland retook Kyiv: on May 7 Polish reconnaissance units rode to the centre of the city by tram, and on May 8 ten regiments of the 3rd Polish Army entered the capital(Citation: Нариси історії Української революції 1917–1921 років: Кн. 2 2012).
The occupier gathered its forces and on June 6 broke through the Polish front south of Kyiv, at Samhorodok. On June 10 the Polish troops, having blown up the Chain and Rusanivskyi bridges, withdrew from Kyiv(Citation: Нариси історії Української революції 1917–1921 років: Кн. 2 2012). On June 12, 1920, Yegorov reported: «Units of the 58th Division have taken Pechersk and are entering Kyiv». The orders to cut the Kyiv - Korosten railway, issued the day before, were signed by Yegorov and Stalin(Citation: Директивы командования фронтов Красной армии (1917–1922). Т. 3 1974).
On October 18, 1920, an armistice took effect on the Polish-Soviet front, and the UNR Army was left to face the invader alone(Citation: Нариси історії Української революції 1917–1921 років: Кн. 2 2012). By November 10 it held the front with 8,968 bayonets and 3,250 sabres, with 95 guns and 687 machine guns. Against it the Soviet command moved the 12th and 14th armies, the Bashkir cavalry brigade and Kotovsky's cavalry brigade: 24,000 bayonets, 4,000 sabres, 120 guns and five armoured trains(Citation: Останні дні збройної боротьби (21.XI.1920 — 21.XI.1930) 1930). The occupation troops attacked first and thwarted the offensive being prepared in Podillia, in today's Vinnytsia and Khmelnytskyi oblasts. In eleven days of fighting the UNR Army lost about 13 thousand soldiers, almost all of its artillery and four armoured trains(Citation: Нариси історії Української революції 1917–1921 років: Кн. 2 2012).
On November 21, 1920, about 12 thousand UNR soldiers, together with the staff of Symon Petliura and the ministries, crossed the Zbruch River, along which ran the border with the lands ceded to Poland under the Treaty of Warsaw(Citation: Нариси історії Української революції 1917–1921 років: Кн. 2 2012). Mykhailo Andrusiak, a participant in the retreat, recalled: «Sadly, with bowed heads, the Cossacks laid down their arms after crossing the bridge and marched on to the West»(Citation: Останній відступ (Спомини М. Андрусяка) 1930).
In the autumn of 1921 the soldiers of the UNR army made a last attempt to raise a general uprising against the Soviet occupiers. This raid is known as the Second Winter Campaign, and its course is known from the report of the chief of the Field Insurgent Staff, Colonel Yurii Otmarshtein, submitted to Symon Petliura. At 2 a.m. on November 4, 1921, the detachment crossed the Polish-Ukrainian border near the village of Borove: 155 officers and officials, 645 Cossacks, 32 horses, with about 56 percent of the men armed with rifles(Citation: До історії повстанчого рейду ген. хор. Ю. Тютюнника в листопаді 1921 р. (Доклад начальника Польового Повстанчого Штабу) 1930). On November 7 the detachment under the overall command of Yurii Tiutiunnyk liberated the Korosten railway junction in battle and freed 600 political prisoners from the jail, but withdrew that same morning: an armoured train of the Soviet occupiers was approaching the town with guns the detachment had nothing to counter, and ammunition had to be spared. Seven officers and twelve Cossacks died in the battle(Citation: До історії повстанчого рейду ген. хор. Ю. Тютюнника в листопаді 1921 р. (Доклад начальника Польового Повстанчого Штабу) 1930).
The detachment could go no further. Half of the infantry marched without boots and with frostbitten feet, the wagon train carried up to 80 wounded, and ammunition was replenished only with what was taken from killed and captured Russians. The staff decided to turn back, towards Poland(Citation: До історії повстанчого рейду ген. хор. Ю. Тютюнника в листопаді 1921 р. (Доклад начальника Польового Повстанчого Штабу) 1930). The troops of the Russian invader blockaded the area of the UNR raid and on November 17 encircled the detachment near the village of Mali Mynky in the north of Zhytomyr Oblast. Over 400 soldiers died in the battle, 537 were taken prisoner, and more than a hundred broke out of the encirclement and crossed the Polish border on November 20(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003)(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004). The prisoners were taken to the village of Bazar, where 359 of them were shot(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963). The armed struggle of the regular UNR Army ended there(Citation: Україна й українці в постімперську добу (1917—1939) 2021).

At 2 a.m. on November 4, 1921, the detachment crossed the Polish-Ukrainian border near the village of Borove: 155 officers and officials, 645 Cossacks, 32 horses, with about 56 percent of the men armed with rifles(Citation: До історії повстанчого рейду ген. хор. Ю. Тютюнника в листопаді 1921 р. (Доклад начальника Польового Повстанчого Штабу) 1930). On November 7 the detachment under the overall command of Yurii Tiutiunnyk liberated the Korosten railway junction in battle and freed 600 political prisoners from the jail, but withdrew that same morning: an armoured train of the Soviet occupiers was approaching the town with guns the detachment had nothing to counter, and ammunition had to be spared. Seven officers and twelve Cossacks died in the battle(Citation: До історії повстанчого рейду ген. хор. Ю. Тютюнника в листопаді 1921 р. (Доклад начальника Польового Повстанчого Штабу) 1930).
The detachment could go no further. Half of the infantry marched without boots and with frostbitten feet, the wagon train carried up to 80 wounded, and ammunition was replenished only with what was taken from killed and captured Russians. The staff decided to turn back, towards Poland(Citation: До історії повстанчого рейду ген. хор. Ю. Тютюнника в листопаді 1921 р. (Доклад начальника Польового Повстанчого Штабу) 1930). The troops of the Russian invader blockaded the area of the UNR raid and on November 17 encircled the detachment near the village of Mali Mynky in the north of Zhytomyr Oblast. Over 400 soldiers died in the battle, 537 were taken prisoner, and more than a hundred broke out of the encirclement and crossed the Polish border on November 20(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003)(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004). The prisoners were taken to the village of Bazar, where 359 of them were shot(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963). The armed struggle of the regular UNR Army ended there(Citation: Україна й українці в постімперську добу (1917—1939) 2021).

objects.description:
In the autumn of 1921 the soldiers of the Army of the Ukrainian People's Republic (UNR), who had retreated across the Zbruch River in November 1920, formed detachments and returned to Ukraine to raise an uprising against Soviet rule. This raid is known as the Second Winter Campaign(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004). On November 17, 1921, occupation troops under the command of Kotovsky encircled the UNR detachment near the village of Mali Mynky in the north of Zhytomyr Oblast(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004).
The captured Ukrainians were taken to the neighbouring village of Bazar and locked in the church. A visiting commission of the Cheka - the secret police of Soviet Russia, predecessor of today's FSB - arrived from Kyiv to judge them; the Communists called it the «Extraordinary Five». Its resolution, signed in Bazar on November 22, 1921, was entered into the collection of orders to the troops of the Kyiv Military District as No. 2578 of November 26, 1921(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The Russian commission described the battle as follows: «Over 400 men were cut down in the battle and 537 captured, including the wounded… In all, 443 men appeared before the extraordinary commission (the Five); the rest died of their wounds before the commission arrived or were in grave condition and left until recovery»(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The commission recorded the motive for the execution in the same document: «Guided by the dictates of revolutionary conscience… and in order to prevent similar crimes… and to show the entire capitalist world and its hirelings that the power of the Soviets mercilessly punishes anyone who attempts to disrupt its peaceful work, the Extraordinary Five resolves: 1. The persons listed in the annex hereto, numbering 359, as malicious, active bandits - TO BE SHOT»(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The fate of the remaining Ukrainian prisoners the commission set out in the same document: forty-one men of the senior command and civil administration it ordered sent for further interrogation by the investigative organs, and forty-two former Red Army soldiers, captured a year earlier, to the special department of the Kyiv Military District for screening(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The resolution was signed by commission chairman Garkavy, members Livshits, Ivanov, Kotovsky and Frinovsky, and secretary Litvinov. Kotovsky, who put his signature under the death sentence, commanded the very troops that had encircled the detachment at Mali Mynky. The order for the district was signed by district commander Yakir, member of the district Revolutionary Military Council Zatonsky, and district chief of staff Pauka(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The Soviet command offered the prisoners a transfer into the Red Army; not one agreed(Citation: Україна й українці в постімперську добу (1917—1939) 2021)(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003). The colonizers carried out the execution in front of people herded to watch: the day before, they forced local peasants to dig a long ditch in a ravine near Bazar, and brought in the residents of the surrounding villages to the execution site(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963). Before the ditch one of the commissars asked once more who wished to join the Red Army. From the ranks came the answer: «We will not serve you!.. Shoot!.. The people will not forgive you for this!»(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963). The condemned embraced and sang «Shche ne vmerla Ukraina» - the song that seventy years later, after Ukraine declared independence in 1991, became the national anthem of Ukraine and remains so to this day(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 10 2013). To the sound of the anthem, Soviet troops shot all 359 Ukrainian prisoners near the village of Bazar(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963)(Citation: Україна й українці в постімперську добу (1917—1939) 2021). The testimonies were gathered by a courier of the Ukrainian underground who visited Mali Mynky and Bazar immediately after the execution(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The exact day of the execution differs between sources, ranging from November 21 to 23(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963)(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003)(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004).
The list of all 359 executed men, name by name, was published by Sotnyk O. Shpilinskyi in Kalisz in 1932; the list was later reprinted together with the text of the resolution(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
Historian Larysa Yakubova writes: «This execution became a tragic symbol of the Ukrainian Revolution of 1917—1921. The armed struggle of the regular UNR Army came to an end»(Citation: Україна й українці в постімперську добу (1917—1939) 2021).

objects.description:
In the autumn of 1921 the soldiers of the Army of the Ukrainian People's Republic (UNR), who had retreated across the Zbruch River in November 1920, formed detachments and returned to Ukraine to raise an uprising against Soviet rule. This raid is known as the Second Winter Campaign(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004). On November 17, 1921, occupation troops under the command of Kotovsky encircled the UNR detachment near the village of Mali Mynky in the north of Zhytomyr Oblast(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004).
The captured Ukrainians were taken to the neighbouring village of Bazar and locked in the church. A visiting commission of the Cheka - the secret police of Soviet Russia, predecessor of today's FSB - arrived from Kyiv to judge them; the Communists called it the «Extraordinary Five». Its resolution, signed in Bazar on November 22, 1921, was entered into the collection of orders to the troops of the Kyiv Military District as No. 2578 of November 26, 1921(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The Russian commission described the battle as follows: «Over 400 men were cut down in the battle and 537 captured, including the wounded… In all, 443 men appeared before the extraordinary commission (the Five); the rest died of their wounds before the commission arrived or were in grave condition and left until recovery»(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The commission recorded the motive for the execution in the same document: «Guided by the dictates of revolutionary conscience… and in order to prevent similar crimes… and to show the entire capitalist world and its hirelings that the power of the Soviets mercilessly punishes anyone who attempts to disrupt its peaceful work, the Extraordinary Five resolves: 1. The persons listed in the annex hereto, numbering 359, as malicious, active bandits - TO BE SHOT»(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The fate of the remaining Ukrainian prisoners the commission set out in the same document: forty-one men of the senior command and civil administration it ordered sent for further interrogation by the investigative organs, and forty-two former Red Army soldiers, captured a year earlier, to the special department of the Kyiv Military District for screening(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The resolution was signed by commission chairman Garkavy, members Livshits, Ivanov, Kotovsky and Frinovsky, and secretary Litvinov. Kotovsky, who put his signature under the death sentence, commanded the very troops that had encircled the detachment at Mali Mynky. The order for the district was signed by district commander Yakir, member of the district Revolutionary Military Council Zatonsky, and district chief of staff Pauka(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The Soviet command offered the prisoners a transfer into the Red Army; not one agreed(Citation: Україна й українці в постімперську добу (1917—1939) 2021)(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003). The colonizers carried out the execution in front of people herded to watch: the day before, they forced local peasants to dig a long ditch in a ravine near Bazar, and brought in the residents of the surrounding villages to the execution site(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963). Before the ditch one of the commissars asked once more who wished to join the Red Army. From the ranks came the answer: «We will not serve you!.. Shoot!.. The people will not forgive you for this!»(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963). The condemned embraced and sang «Shche ne vmerla Ukraina» - the song that seventy years later, after Ukraine declared independence in 1991, became the national anthem of Ukraine and remains so to this day(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 10 2013). To the sound of the anthem, Soviet troops shot all 359 Ukrainian prisoners near the village of Bazar(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963)(Citation: Україна й українці в постімперську добу (1917—1939) 2021). The testimonies were gathered by a courier of the Ukrainian underground who visited Mali Mynky and Bazar immediately after the execution(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The exact day of the execution differs between sources, ranging from November 21 to 23(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963)(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003)(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004).
The list of all 359 executed men, name by name, was published by Sotnyk O. Shpilinskyi in Kalisz in 1932; the list was later reprinted together with the text of the resolution(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
Historian Larysa Yakubova writes: «This execution became a tragic symbol of the Ukrainian Revolution of 1917—1921. The armed struggle of the regular UNR Army came to an end»(Citation: Україна й українці в постімперську добу (1917—1939) 2021).

objects.description:
In the autumn of 1921 the soldiers of the Army of the Ukrainian People's Republic (UNR), who had retreated across the Zbruch River in November 1920, formed detachments and returned to Ukraine to raise an uprising against Soviet rule. This raid is known as the Second Winter Campaign(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004). On November 17, 1921, occupation troops under the command of Kotovsky encircled the UNR detachment near the village of Mali Mynky in the north of Zhytomyr Oblast(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004).
The captured Ukrainians were taken to the neighbouring village of Bazar and locked in the church. A visiting commission of the Cheka - the secret police of Soviet Russia, predecessor of today's FSB - arrived from Kyiv to judge them; the Communists called it the «Extraordinary Five». Its resolution, signed in Bazar on November 22, 1921, was entered into the collection of orders to the troops of the Kyiv Military District as No. 2578 of November 26, 1921(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The Russian commission described the battle as follows: «Over 400 men were cut down in the battle and 537 captured, including the wounded… In all, 443 men appeared before the extraordinary commission (the Five); the rest died of their wounds before the commission arrived or were in grave condition and left until recovery»(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The commission recorded the motive for the execution in the same document: «Guided by the dictates of revolutionary conscience… and in order to prevent similar crimes… and to show the entire capitalist world and its hirelings that the power of the Soviets mercilessly punishes anyone who attempts to disrupt its peaceful work, the Extraordinary Five resolves: 1. The persons listed in the annex hereto, numbering 359, as malicious, active bandits - TO BE SHOT»(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The fate of the remaining Ukrainian prisoners the commission set out in the same document: forty-one men of the senior command and civil administration it ordered sent for further interrogation by the investigative organs, and forty-two former Red Army soldiers, captured a year earlier, to the special department of the Kyiv Military District for screening(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The resolution was signed by commission chairman Garkavy, members Livshits, Ivanov, Kotovsky and Frinovsky, and secretary Litvinov. Kotovsky, who put his signature under the death sentence, commanded the very troops that had encircled the detachment at Mali Mynky. The order for the district was signed by district commander Yakir, member of the district Revolutionary Military Council Zatonsky, and district chief of staff Pauka(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).
The Soviet command offered the prisoners a transfer into the Red Army; not one agreed(Citation: Україна й українці в постімперську добу (1917—1939) 2021)(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003). The colonizers carried out the execution in front of people herded to watch: the day before, they forced local peasants to dig a long ditch in a ravine near Bazar, and brought in the residents of the surrounding villages to the execution site(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963). Before the ditch one of the commissars asked once more who wished to join the Red Army. From the ranks came the answer: «We will not serve you!.. Shoot!.. The people will not forgive you for this!»(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963). The condemned embraced and sang «Shche ne vmerla Ukraina» - the song that seventy years later, after Ukraine declared independence in 1991, became the national anthem of Ukraine and remains so to this day(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 10 2013). The testimonies were gathered by a courier of the Ukrainian underground who visited Mali Mynky and Bazar immediately after the execution(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).

The list of all 359 executed men, name by name, was published by Sotnyk O. Shpilinskyi in Kalisz in 1932; the list was later reprinted together with the text of the resolution(Citation: Вигнати окупанта 1963).

The resolution of the Council of People's Commissars of the Ukrainian SSR and the CC of the CP(b)U of December 6, 1932, signed by Chubar and Kosior, prescribed "the immediate cessation of the delivery of goods, the complete cessation of cooperative and state trade on site, and the removal of all available goods from the respective cooperative and state shops," as well as "a complete ban on kolkhoz trade both for kolkhozes and kolkhoz members and for individual farmers"(Citation: О занесении на черную доску сел, злостно саботирующих хлебозаготовки 1932).

objects.description: Sealing off the starving region: peasants who tried to escape from the blockaded villages were intercepted on roads and at railway junctions. The directive sealed off precisely Ukraine and the Kuban: "all peasants who had managed to leave Ukraine and the North Caucasus were subject to return to their places of residence," while permits to leave were denied even "to the national districts of the krai, where there was no famine at all"(Citation: Відносини держави, суспільства і особи під час створення радянського ладу в Україні (1917 – 1938 рр.) 2013). Within 50 days "219.5 thousand peasants were detained, including 38 thousand in the Ukrainian SSR, 47 thousand in the North Caucasus, 44 thousand in the Central Black Earth region, 5 thousand in the Western oblast, 65 thousand on the railways"; of these, "186.5 thousand were sent home under convoy, almost 3 thousand were convicted, and all the rest awaited trial or were under investigation in filtration camps"(Citation: Відносини держави, суспільства і особи під час створення радянського ладу в Україні (1917 – 1938 рр.) 2013). The point of the operation lay not in sentences but in marching people back into the starving villages: the coded telegram "documentarily attests to his intention to organize absolute famine in the rural areas of Ukraine"(Citation: Відносини держави, суспільства і особи під час створення радянського ладу в Україні (1917 – 1938 рр.) 2013).

objects.description: Sealing off the starving region: peasants who tried to escape from the blockaded villages were intercepted on roads and at railway junctions. The directive sealed off precisely Ukraine and the Kuban: "all peasants who had managed to leave Ukraine and the North Caucasus were subject to return to their places of residence," while permits to leave were denied even "to the national districts of the krai, where there was no famine at all"(Citation: Відносини держави, суспільства і особи під час створення радянського ладу в Україні (1917 – 1938 рр.) 2013). Within 50 days "219.5 thousand peasants were detained, including 38 thousand in the Ukrainian SSR, 47 thousand in the North Caucasus, 44 thousand in the Central Black Earth region, 5 thousand in the Western oblast, 65 thousand on the railways"; of these, "186.5 thousand were sent home under convoy, almost 3 thousand were convicted, and all the rest awaited trial or were under investigation in filtration camps"(Citation: Відносини держави, суспільства і особи під час створення радянського ладу в Україні (1917 – 1938 рр.) 2013). The point of the operation lay not in sentences but in marching people back into the starving villages: the coded telegram "documentarily attests to his intention to organize absolute famine in the rural areas of Ukraine"(Citation: Відносини держави, суспільства і особи під час створення радянського ладу в Україні (1917 – 1938 рр.) 2013).

Grekov, K. Huslystyi, and F. Yastrebov, "of Kyivan Rus as the 'common cradle' of the history of the Ukrainian, Russian, and Belarusian peoples," and "in 1939 B. Grekov advanced the proposition of the ethnic unity of the 'Rus people' in the era of Kyivan Rus"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004). This scheme displaced M. Hrushevsky's conception and denied the independence of Ukraine's history.

objects.description: The conduct of secret mass "national operations" of the NKVD for the physical annihilation of members of ethnic minorities(Citation: В тени «Большого Брата»: Западные национальные меньшинства в СССР (1917-1938 гг.) 2011). The mechanism was set by the operational orders of people's commissar Yezhov: No. 00485 of 11 August 1937 opened the Polish operation - "to begin, from 20 August 1937, a broad operation aimed at the complete liquidation of the local organizations of the 'POW'" with completion "within a three-month term"(Citation: Оперативный приказ НКВД СССР № 00485 1937), - and No. 00439 of 25 July 1937 the German one(Citation: Оперативный приказ НКВД СССР № 00439 1937); the Greek, Bulgarian and other operations followed their template(Citation: В тени «Большого Брата»: Западные национальные меньшинства в СССР (1917-1938 гг.) 2011). The scale is recorded in the perpetrator's own accounting: according to the summary figures of the 1st Special Department of the NKVD of the Ukrainian SSR dated 30 August 1938, 94,659 people were arrested in the republic under orders Nos. 00485, 00593 and others (54,011 on the Polish line, 23,036 on the German, 5,642 on the Greek), of whom 61,683 had been convicted by 1 July 1938; in all, of the 197,945 people convicted by the NKVD of the Ukrainian SSR over the reporting period, 122,274 were sentenced to be shot - nearly two out of every three(Citation: Сводные данные об арестованных и осужденных органами НКВД УССР за время с 1 октября 1936 года по 1-е июля 1938 года 1938). Across all the "national lines" of the USSR, 335,513 people were convicted, and 73.66% of them were shot(Citation: Національне питання в Україні ХХ – початку ХХІ ст. 2012).

objects.description: The conduct of secret mass "national operations" of the NKVD for the physical annihilation of members of ethnic minorities(Citation: В тени «Большого Брата»: Западные национальные меньшинства в СССР (1917-1938 гг.) 2011). The mechanism was set by the operational orders of people's commissar Yezhov: No. 00485 of 11 August 1937 opened the Polish operation - "to begin, from 20 August 1937, a broad operation aimed at the complete liquidation of the local organizations of the 'POW'" with completion "within a three-month term"(Citation: Оперативный приказ НКВД СССР № 00485 1937), - and No. 00439 of 25 July 1937 the German one(Citation: Оперативный приказ НКВД СССР № 00439 1937); the Greek, Bulgarian and other operations followed their template(Citation: В тени «Большого Брата»: Западные национальные меньшинства в СССР (1917-1938 гг.) 2011). The scale is recorded in the perpetrator's own accounting: according to the summary figures of the 1st Special Department of the NKVD of the Ukrainian SSR dated 30 August 1938, 94,659 people were arrested in the republic under orders Nos. 00485, 00593 and others (54,011 on the Polish line, 23,036 on the German, 5,642 on the Greek), of whom 61,683 had been convicted by 1 July 1938; in all, of the 197,945 people convicted by the NKVD of the Ukrainian SSR over the reporting period, 122,274 were sentenced to be shot - nearly two out of every three(Citation: Сводные данные об арестованных и осужденных органами НКВД УССР за время с 1 октября 1936 года по 1-е июля 1938 года 1938). Across all the "national lines" of the USSR, 335,513 people were convicted, and 73.66% of them were shot(Citation: Національне питання в Україні ХХ – початку ХХІ ст. 2012).

objects.description: On 24 January 1938 the Orgburo of the Central Committee of the VKP(b), by its resolution "On the Liquidation of National Schools and National Sections in Schools," closed non-Russian schools throughout the Union, liquidating the national districts and village soviets on the same day(Citation: О ликвидации национальных школ и национальных отделений в школах 1938)(Citation: О ликвидации национальных районов и сельсоветов 1938); on 13 March the resolution of the Central Committee of the VKP(b) and the USSR Council of People's Commissars No. 324 "On the Compulsory Study of the Russian Language in the Schools of the National Republics and Regions" made the metropole's language a compulsory subject in all schools of the republics(Citation: Об обязательном изучении русского языка в школах национальных республик и областей 1938). Kyiv executed the decision on 10 April 1938: the Politburo of the Central Committee of the KP(b)U, "proceeding from the decision of the Central Committee of the VKP(b)," declared "the further existence of special national schools inexpedient and harmful" and resolved to reorganize the German, Polish, Czech, Swedish and other schools and technical colleges "into Soviet schools of the ordinary type," to liquidate national sections and classes at ordinary schools, colleges and universities, and, where there was nowhere to transfer the pupils, to transfer the institutions themselves to ordinary school curricula - "with instruction in Ukrainian or Russian"; the Odesa German Pedagogical Institute was turned into an institute of foreign languages, and all the work was ordered finished by 1 August 1938(Citation: Німці в Україні. 20—30-ті рр. XX ст. 1994). The Politburo wrote its justification into the resolution itself: "enemies of the people - Trotskyites, Bukharinites and bourgeois nationalists operating in the People's Commissariat of Education of the Ukrainian SSR - implanted special national German, Polish, Czech, Swedish, Greek and other schools, turning them into hotbeds of bourgeois-nationalist, anti-Soviet influence on children"(Citation: Німці в Україні. 20—30-ті рр. XX ст. 1994). The decision was given the form of a state act by the Council of People's Commissars of the Ukrainian SSR in its resolution of 29 June 1938 on the reorganization of special national schools, colleges and the Odesa German Pedagogical Institute: by 1 August 1938, 766 national primary, incomplete secondary and secondary schools were subject to reorganization into ordinary schools with (predominantly) Russian and Ukrainian as the language of instruction, and another 122 were merged with Russian and Ukrainian ones on the territorial principle - the count of the historian Liudmyla Yakubova(Citation: Національно-культурне життя етнічних меншостей України ( 20-30-ті роки ): коренізація і денаціоналізація (2) 1999).

objects.description: On 24 January 1938 the Orgburo of the Central Committee of the VKP(b), by its resolution "On the Liquidation of National Schools and National Sections in Schools," closed non-Russian schools throughout the Union, liquidating the national districts and village soviets on the same day(Citation: О ликвидации национальных школ и национальных отделений в школах 1938)(Citation: О ликвидации национальных районов и сельсоветов 1938); on 13 March the resolution of the Central Committee of the VKP(b) and the USSR Council of People's Commissars No. 324 "On the Compulsory Study of the Russian Language in the Schools of the National Republics and Regions" made the metropole's language a compulsory subject in all schools of the republics(Citation: Об обязательном изучении русского языка в школах национальных республик и областей 1938). Kyiv executed the decision on 10 April 1938: the Politburo of the Central Committee of the KP(b)U, "proceeding from the decision of the Central Committee of the VKP(b)," declared "the further existence of special national schools inexpedient and harmful" and resolved to reorganize the German, Polish, Czech, Swedish and other schools and technical colleges "into Soviet schools of the ordinary type," to liquidate national sections and classes at ordinary schools, colleges and universities, and, where there was nowhere to transfer the pupils, to transfer the institutions themselves to ordinary school curricula - "with instruction in Ukrainian or Russian"; the Odesa German Pedagogical Institute was turned into an institute of foreign languages, and all the work was ordered finished by 1 August 1938(Citation: Німці в Україні. 20—30-ті рр. XX ст. 1994). The Politburo wrote its justification into the resolution itself: "enemies of the people - Trotskyites, Bukharinites and bourgeois nationalists operating in the People's Commissariat of Education of the Ukrainian SSR - implanted special national German, Polish, Czech, Swedish, Greek and other schools, turning them into hotbeds of bourgeois-nationalist, anti-Soviet influence on children"(Citation: Німці в Україні. 20—30-ті рр. XX ст. 1994). The decision was given the form of a state act by the Council of People's Commissars of the Ukrainian SSR in its resolution of 29 June 1938 on the reorganization of special national schools, colleges and the Odesa German Pedagogical Institute: by 1 August 1938, 766 national primary, incomplete secondary and secondary schools were subject to reorganization into ordinary schools with (predominantly) Russian and Ukrainian as the language of instruction, and another 122 were merged with Russian and Ukrainian ones on the territorial principle - the count of the historian Liudmyla Yakubova(Citation: Національно-культурне життя етнічних меншостей України ( 20-30-ті роки ): коренізація і денаціоналізація (2) 1999).

objects.description: The partition of Eastern Europe behind the backs of its peoples: the secret protocol established that "in the event of a territorial-political rearrangement of the areas belonging to the Polish state, the boundary of the spheres of interest of Germany and the USSR shall run approximately along the line of the rivers Narew, Vistula, and San"(Citation: Секретный дополнительный протокол к Договору о ненападении между Германией и СССР 1939). Half a century later the Congress of People's Deputies of the USSR "recognizes the secret protocols as legally untenable and invalid from the moment of their signing"(Citation: Постановление Съезда народных депутатов СССР о секретных протоколах 1989). objects.description: Mass forced resettlement by quota: "under the resolutions of the Council of People's Commissars of December 5, 1939 and March 2, 1940, subject to administrative resettlement were the employees of the former state institutions, courts, police, army, merchants, Polish settlers, landowners, owners of plants and factories, and their families"; in total "up to 1,250,000 people were removed to remote regions of the USSR"(Citation: Депортація (Енциклопедія Сучасної України) 2007). The waves were separate: the osadniks were deported under the USSR Sovnarkom resolution of December 5, 1939, no. 2010-558ss - its text remains in the closed Archive of the President of the Russian Federation (fond 93), while the mechanics of the operation are known from the NKVD Instruction approved on December 29, 1939(Citation: Инструкция НКВД СССР о порядке переселения польских осадников из западных областей УССР и БССР (утв. пост. objects.description: The sign of the new order goes up within the very first weeks: Soviet troops took Lviv on 22 September 1939(Citation: «Радянізація» Львова: вересень 1939 - червень 1941 рр. 2026), and already in October, in the city center, on the islet in the middle of today's Svobody Avenue, rose the monument to the Stalin Constitution - a huge vertical composition of columns entwined with red banners, on a wooden frame, with five sculptural groups (a Red Army soldier, a worker, a mother with a child, a female student, and an old Hutsul with a boy) and inscriptions in Ukrainian, Polish and Yiddish symbolizing the "friendship of peoples" according to the articles of the Stalin constitution(Citation: Zapomniany pomnik 2012)(Citation: View on the Monument to the Soviet Constitution, Lviv 1940 (REESOURCES) 2026). The sign has named authors: the sculptor Serhii Lytvynenko and the Kyiv artist Mykhailo Dmytrenko, who arrived in Lviv in 1939 in the "landing party" of Soviet artists whose task was the implantation of socialist realism; possibly the authors merely adapted to the site a design produced in Moscow, and it was executed by the sculptors Yevhen Dzyndra and Andrii Koverko(Citation: Zapomniany pomnik 2012). The monument stood until 30 June 1941 and vanished with the arrival of the Germans(Citation: Zapomniany pomnik 2012).

objects.description: The use of untrained conscripts as expendable material: they were "thrown into combat often at once, without undergoing military training in reserve units, sometimes unarmed, not even changed into military uniform (hence the name)"(Citation: «Чорна піхота» як історичне явище 2019). The scale is visible from a single episode: "after the Red Army first took Kharkiv in the spring of 1943, about 15 thousand people aged 15 to 45 were mobilized into it and sent to the front without training," with "1 rifle per 5-10 men"(Citation: «Чорна піхота» як історичне явище 2019).

objects.description: Regular chekist-military operations by the NKVD and MGB to sweep western Ukrainian villages: the People's Commissar of Internal Affairs of the Ukrainian SSR T. Strokach personally "directed and coordinated operational-chekist operations to liquidate the underground of the Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists and units of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, and mass deportations of the population in Western Ukraine"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 9 2012). objects.description: Extrajudicial killings of civilians in the course of suppressing the insurgency: the Presidium of the CPSU Central Committee itself admitted, in its resolution "On the Political and Economic Situation of the Western Oblasts of the Ukrainian SSR" of May 26, 1953: "From 1944 through 1952, up to 500 thousand people in the western oblasts of Ukraine were subjected to various kinds of repression, including over 134 thousand arrested, over 153 thousand killed, and over 203 thousand deported forever from the Ukrainian SSR"(Citation: Постановление Президиума ЦК КПСС «О политическом и хозяйственном состоянии западных областей Украинской ССР» 1953)(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004) – the authorities did not divide the killed into insurgents and civilians, and already on July 2, 1953, after Beria's arrest, the resolution itself was revoked as conducive to "the activization of bourgeois-nationalist elements"(Citation: Постановление Президиума ЦК КПСС «О политическом и хозяйственном состоянии западных областей Украинской ССР» 1953). Terror was also waged by disguised MGB "special groups" acting under the guise of the UPA: the military prosecutor of the MVD troops of the Ukrainian district, Kosharsky, in his report to Khrushchev (February 15, 1949), cited "examples of beatings, rapes and robberies of the population" by agent-fighters and stated: "the actions of the so-called MGB special groups are of a pronounced bandit, anti-Soviet character and, of course, cannot be justified by any operational considerations"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011).

objects.description: The creation of an atmosphere of total fear through the bloody provocations of NKVD special groups operating in the guise of the UPA: People's Commissar Strokach "initiated the formation of special groups of the NKVD of the Ukrainian SSR from former partisans for the struggle against the UPA" and "personally interrogated the captured leaders of the OUN networks of Western Ukraine"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 9 2012). The terror was also demonstrative: "one of the forms of struggle was the policy of intimidating OUN and UPA members and the local population: open trials and executions, putting the bodies of the dead on public display, and destroying insurgent graves"(Citation: Рух Опору у Карпатському краї (1940–1950 рр.): тексти лекцій (Ільницький) 2024).

objects.description: The forcible removal of insurgents' families to Siberia and the deportation of the Ukrainians of Zakerzonnia: the removal of "bandit accomplices" with their entire families began at once - already in the summer of 1944 "more than 17,000 people were carried off to Krasnoyarsk Krai"(Citation: Депортація (Енциклопедія Сучасної України) 2007); in all, in 1944–52, 203,662 people were removed to special settlements, among them "representatives of the families of members of the Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists and soldiers of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army and their sympathizers — 182,543 people"(Citation: Депортація (Енциклопедія Сучасної України) 2007). Operation "Vistula" was carried out in order to "deprive it of socio-economic and moral-psychological support from the local Ukrainian population," and ended in the scattering of the community: the authorities rid themselves of the Ukrainian population, "dispersing about 150 thousand people"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003).

objects.description: Mass arrests of UPA fighters, OUN members, and those suspected of aiding them, followed by dispatch to the GULAG camps, upon which the regime placed "the isolation of 'unreliable elements'" as one of its key tasks(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004). During Operation "Vistula," for civilians suspected of assisting the underground there was provision for "the introduction of courts-martial and concentration camps, in particular at Jaworzno"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003). By 1951 Ukrainians had become the second-largest nation of the GULAG: according to the agency's own statistics, the "National composition of GULAG prisoners (as of January 1, 1951)" counted 506,221 Ukrainians out of some 2.5 million prisoners - about 20%(Citation: ГУЛАГ (историко-социологический аспект) (Земсков) 1991).

objects.description: A state campaign to construct a historical myth: the "Theses on the 300th Anniversary of the Reunification of Ukraine with Russia," approved by the CPSU Central Committee, declared that "by this historic act was completed the long struggle of the freedom-loving Ukrainian people against foreign enslavers for reunification with the Russian people in a single Russian state"(Citation: Приєднання чи возз'єднання? 1972) – the annexation of 1654 was retroactively rewritten as the goal and outcome of a national struggle.

objects.description: The imposition of a concept of unbreakable unity instead of recognizing a distinct nation: per the Theses, "by the act of reunification the Ukrainian people consolidated its close and unbreakable historical bond with the Russian people, in whom it found a great ally, a faithful friend and defender"(Citation: Приєднання чи возз'єднання? 1972). The celebrations and the transfer of Crimea "taking into account the commonality of the economy, territorial proximity, and close economic and cultural ties"(Citation: Указ о передаче Крымской области из состава РСФСР в состав УССР 1954) served the same frame.

objects.description: The redrawing of internal borders by the USSR Supreme Soviet Presidium's resolution of 19 February 1954: "To approve the joint submission of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the RSFSR and the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the Ukrainian SSR on the transfer of the Crimean oblast from the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic to the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic"(Citation: Указ о передаче Крымской области из состава РСФСР в состав УССР 1954) – the decision was taken in Moscow, without any expression of will by the peninsula's inhabitants. Behind the "commonality of the economy" stood the desire to shift the peninsula, ruined by deportation and war, onto the books of the Ukrainian SSR: "Moscow admits ever more openly: the Crimean region is a problem territory that the union center does not know how to sustain"(Citation: Подарунок Хрущова — Крим у складі Української РСР — що насправді відбулося у 1954 році (Суспільне) 2026).

objects.description: The jubilee was fixed with a material sign in Pereiaslav in the Kyiv region, on the very square where the rada had taken place in 1654. The sign went up in the course of the jubilee reconstruction of the town ordered by the republic's authorities: "in connection with the preparation for the celebration of the 300th anniversary of the reunification of Ukraine with Russia," the Council of Ministers of the Ukrainian SSR allocated 20 million rubles for the reconstruction of Pereiaslav-Khmelnytskyi, the reconstruction plan was developed under the direction of the architect Volodymyr Zabolotnyi, and in May 1954, "on the square where the historic Pereiaslav Rada took place (now Reunification Square), an obelisk with a memorial plaque was put up"(Citation: Історія міст і сіл Української РСР. Київська область 1971). On the plaque, beneath a relief of Bohdan Khmelnytsky, a text is cast: "On this square, on 8 (18) January 1654, the Pereiaslav Rada took place, which, expressing the will of the Ukrainian people, unanimously adopted the historic decision on the reunification of Ukraine with Russia"(Citation: Пам'ятний знак на честь 300-річчя Переяславської Ради, обеліск на площі Переяславської Ради 2014). The sign did not merely mark the spot: it declared the decision unanimous and expressive of the people's will, fixing this version in bronze on the very square where it all happened.

objects.description: The forced disappearance of a key functionary of the movement: "on the night of January 15–16, 1994, two armed unknown men burst into the NRU secretariat in Kyiv, took some documents, and searched for Boichyshyn" - Mykhailo Boichyshyn, head of the Rukh secretariat, was never seen again. The investigation was sabotaged: law enforcement "at first was in no hurry to accept the report of the politician's disappearance, and then demonstratively displayed disinterest in solving the crime," and "the investigators were interested not so much in the circumstances of the attack on the Secretariat and Boichyshyn's disappearance as in the party's financing"(Citation: Михайло Бойчишин — голова Секретаріату НРУ (Український погляд) 2024).

objects.description: An armed seizure of power: the GKChP statement of 18 August 1991 announced the transfer of the USSR president's powers: "In connection with the impossibility, for reasons of health, of Mikhail Sergeevich Gorbachev performing the duties of President of the USSR and the transfer… of the powers of the President of the USSR to Vice-President Gennady Ivanovich Yanayev… to form the State Committee for the State of Emergency in the USSR"(Citation: Заявление ГКЧП 1991). The putsch was timed to derail the treaty-based reconstitution of the Union: "The formation of the GKChP was preceded by the so-called Novo-Ogaryovo process - negotiations begun on April 23, 1991 by USSR President Gorbachev at his suburban residence of Novo-Ogaryovo with the leaders of the union republics on the signing of a new Union Treaty"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Додатковий том 2021) - the coup cut this process short.

objects.description: The conduct of an aggressive information campaign in favor of "their" candidate with the direct participation of the head of the Russian state: live on three Ukrainian television channels two weeks before the vote, praise was voiced for the candidate's government - "V. Yanukovych's government achieved more: they managed to fill this growth with good quality. That is, Ukraine's economy is developing in a diversified way"(Citation: Прямая линия с жителями Украины 2004). In parallel, opponents were demonized with accusations of nationalism and pro-fascist views.

objects.description: The instigation of the threat of splitting the country in response to the protests: at the congress in Sievierodonetsk on November 28, 2004, Regions faction leader R. Bohatyriova gave a direct promise of a separatist referendum - "we will not go to it with you, we will hold a referendum on the creation of a South-Eastern state (ovation, applause)"(Citation: Стенограмма Северодонецкого съезда 2004). The presence of Russian officials lent this Moscow's sanction: the mayor of Moscow Yu. Luzhkov reminded the hall from the rostrum that "our President of Russia Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin was the first to congratulate Viktor Fedorovych Yanukovych on his victory"(Citation: Стенограмма Северодонецкого съезда 2004).

objects.description: Direct energy blackmail and the cut-off of gas supplies at the height of winter: on January 1, 2006 - "at 10.00am Moscow time on January 1, 2006, Gazprom cut off gas supplies to Ukraine"(Citation: The Russian-Ukrainian gas crisis of January 2006 2006); on January 1, 2009 - "Russian exports to Ukraine were cut off on 1 January," after which exports to the EU were "drastically reduced on 6 January and cut completely from 7 January," and in the worst-affected Balkan countries a humanitarian emergency ensued, with "parts of the populations unable to heat their homes"(Citation: The Russo-Ukrainian gas dispute of January 2009 2009).

objects.description: The imposition of corrupt gas-supply schemes through intermediary companies: Moscow "used a series of intermediary trading companies (Itera from 1998, Eural Trans Gas from 2003, Rosukrenergo (RUE) from 2005) to transport, and sometimes to supply, the gas to Ukraine," a practice that "was long criticized in European government circles and by corporate governance bodies (where there was concern about their opacity)"(Citation: The Russo-Ukrainian gas dispute of January 2009 2009). RUE's co-owner Dmytro Firtash told the US ambassador in December 2008 outright that "He acknowledged ties to Russian organized crime figure Seymon Mogilevich, stating he needed Mogilevich's approval to get into business in the first place"(Citation: Cable 08KYIV2414: Firtash makes his case to the USG 2008).

objects.description: An attempt to strike a deal with the US leader over Kyiv's head in order to block Ukraine's Euro-Atlantic integration under the threat of its dismemberment: Ukraine's accession to NATO would create "a field of conflict for you and us, long-term confrontation," while Moscow, relying on anti-NATO forces, "would be working on stripping NATO of the possibility of enlarging. Russia would be creating problems there all the time"(Citation: Memorandum of Conversation: Meeting with President of Russia (Sochi) 2008). As retold by Kommersant's source from the summit itself: "You understand, George, that Ukraine is not even a state! What is Ukraine? Part of its territory is Eastern Europe, and part - a considerable part - was gifted by us!" - with a transparent hint "that Russia could begin the severance of Crimea and Eastern Ukraine"(Citation: Блок НАТО разошелся на блокпакеты (Коммерсантъ) 2008).

objects.description: The deliberate injection of false historical narratives into the international arena: Ukraine, according to the Russian leader, "is not a nation built in a natural manner" and "an artificial country created back in Soviet times," and its territories were supposedly gifts - "In the 1920s and 1930s Ukraine obtained territory from Russia -- that's the eastern part of the country. In 1956, the Crimean peninsula was transferred to Ukraine"(Citation: Memorandum of Conversation: Meeting with President of Russia (Sochi) 2008). From this the thesis of its possible disintegration was derived: "the country could just split apart"(Citation: Memorandum of Conversation: Meeting with President of Russia (Sochi) 2008).

objects.description: The use of economic blackmail and promises of a loan together with a gas discount to coerce V. Yanukovych into derailing the signing of the Association Agreement with the EU: on December 17, 2013, a reduction of the gas price "to 268.5 dollars per thousand cubic meters" (instead of 410) was announced, along with the fact that "Ukraine, under the bilateral agreements, will receive 15 billion dollars from the Russian National Welfare Fund, selling Moscow its government securities for that amount." Putin stressed: "We consider this a temporary solution, bearing in mind that long-term, long-lasting agreements must and will be reached"(Citation: Виктор Янукович и Владимир Путин достигли компромисса в Москве 2013).

objects.description: The use of regular troops without insignia to establish control over the peninsula. A year later V. Putin admitted it on his call-in show of 17 April 2014: "behind the backs of Crimea's self-defense forces, our servicemen, of course, stood. They acted very correctly, but… decisively and professionally"(Citation: Прямая линия с Владимиром Путиным 2014). Ukrainian garrisons on the peninsula were blockaded and disarmed, as Putin himself admitted: "and the way the Ukrainian units were disarmed - all of this was done so swiftly that it seemed it had been prepared for an incredibly long time"(Citation: Прямая линия с Владимиром Путиным 2014).

objects.description: The installation of a controlled administration under military cover: the decisions of the Crimean parliament were taken in conditions where "behind the backs of Crimea's self-defense forces, our servicemen, of course, stood"(Citation: Прямая линия с Владимиром Путиным 2014). The UN General Assembly declared the ensuing referendum void and confirmed that it "was not authorized by Ukraine"(Citation: Territorial integrity of Ukraine (A/RES/68/262) 2014). OHCHR recorded the "election" scene itself: overnight into 27 February "armed groups without insignia took over the buildings of the local government and parliament," and "on 27 February, members of the Parliament of Crimea, in the presence of gunmen, dismissed the local Government and elected Sergey Aksenov as the Head of Crimea"(Citation: Situation of human rights in the temporarily occupied Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol (OHCHR) 2017).

objects.description: The seizure of Sloviansk by an armed group that had crossed the border, and the formation of the separatist "DNR"/"LNR": the detachment's commander openly admitted that "in practice it was our detachment that set in motion the flywheel of the war that is still going on," and that "it was I, after all, who pulled the trigger of the war"(Citation: Стрелков: Спусковой крючок войны нажал я 2014). In parallel, "groups of armed men unlawfully carried out a well-organized and coordinated seizure of public buildings and police and security service offices"(Citation: Доклад Верховного комиссара ООН по правам человека о положении в области прав человека в Украине (A/HRC/27/75) 2014). The "republic's" leadership was from the outset dispatched from Moscow: "Alexander Boroday - the first prime minister of the DNR, who in 2014 handed over his powers to Alexander Zakharchenko," a Muscovite raised "in an intelligentsia Moscow family"(Citation: Александр Бородай: я могу вернуться, но не на Донбасс, а уже в Киев (АиФ) 2016). In the spring and summer of 2014 the same formations tried to take Mariupol: "those advancing on Mariupol were mainly 'vacationers'," that is, Russian soldiers, and about the outcome the same commander says that after their departure "both the front line and the opportunities remained shaky"(Citation: Стрелков: Спусковой крючок войны нажал я 2014); on 13 June Ukrainian troops retook the city.

objects.description: A massive campaign of fabricating fakes to dehumanize Ukrainians: on state television it was claimed that "Ukrainian armed forces herded city residents to the central square and publicly executed a small boy and his mother," yet "there is no evidence to support Pyshniak's claim," and the residents of Sloviansk who were interviewed did not confirm the story(Citation: Fake: Crucifixion in Slovyansk 2014). The same method produced the fabricated "death of a 10-year-old girl" in the Petrovskyi district of Donetsk (March 2015): BBC correspondents on the ground established that no such girl had ever existed(Citation: Би Би Си разоблачили ложь российских СМИ о якобы погибшей 10-летней девочке (StopFake) 2015). In parallel ran an operation to conceal responsibility for the destruction of flight MH17: the Russian Ministry of Defense "made a series of self-contradictory claims blaming Ukraine, rather than Russia or Russian-led separatists, for the Boeing 777's shoot down," while a deputy defense minister publicly repeated "a fabricated claim that originated on Twitter of how a Spanish air traffic controller named Carlos saw two Ukrainian fighter jets near MH17"(Citation: The Kremlin's Shifting, Self-Contradicting Narratives on MH17 2019).

external_references.description: StopFake. Fake: Crucifixion in Slovyansk. 2014.

objects.description: A massive campaign of fabricating fakes to dehumanize Ukrainians: on state television it was claimed that "Ukrainian armed forces herded city residents to the central square and publicly executed a small boy and his mother," yet "there is no evidence to support Pyshniak's claim," and the residents of Sloviansk who were interviewed did not confirm the story(Citation: Fake: Crucifixion in Slovyansk 2014). The same method produced the fabricated "death of a 10-year-old girl" in the Petrovskyi district of Donetsk (March 2015): BBC correspondents on the ground established that no such girl had ever existed(Citation: Би Би Си разоблачили ложь российских СМИ о якобы погибшей 10-летней девочке (StopFake) 2015). In parallel ran an operation to conceal responsibility for the destruction of flight MH17: the Russian Ministry of Defense "made a series of self-contradictory claims blaming Ukraine, rather than Russia or Russian-led separatists, for the Boeing 777's shoot down," while a deputy defense minister publicly repeated "a fabricated claim that originated on Twitter of how a Spanish air traffic controller named Carlos saw two Ukrainian fighter jets near MH17"(Citation: The Kremlin's Shifting, Self-Contradicting Narratives on MH17 2019).

objects.description: The use of a hacker group linked to the security services to compromise Ukrainian artillerymen's software: "the filename 'Попр-Д30.apk' was linked to a legitimate application which was initially developed domestically within Ukraine by an officer of the 55th Artillery Brigade named Yaroslav Sherstuk," and "in-depth reverse engineering revealed the APK contained an Android variant of X-Agent" - an implant whose exclusive operator is FANCY BEAR(Citation: Danger Close: Fancy Bear Tracking of Ukrainian Field Artillery Units 2016). The same toolkit was used in cyberattacks on the Ukrainian power grid in the winters of 2015 and 2016(Citation: 2015 Ukraine Electric Power Attack | MITRE ATT&CK® 2023)(Citation: 2016 Ukraine Electric Power Attack | MITRE ATT&CK® 2023).

objects.description: The overt crossing of the state border by regular Russian troops in the summer and autumn of 2014 to save the separatists from defeat: the "DNR" commander admitted that the decisive role was played by Russian servicemen who came "on leave" - "it was mostly 'vacationers' who advanced on Mariupol. When they left, both the front line and the opportunities became precarious"(Citation: Стрелков: Спусковой крючок войны нажал я 2014). The offensive resulted in heavy losses for the Ukrainian army near Ilovaisk and Debaltseve. The presence of regular troops continued into 2015: the GRU men captured near Shchastia were "soldiers of the 3rd Separate Guards Special Purpose Brigade of the Main Directorate of the General Staff of the Russian Armed Forces, who arrived on the territory of Ukraine on March 26 and were quartered in Luhansk"(Citation: «Короче, разведка — россияне». Как искали, судили и защищали капитана Ерофеева и сержанта Александрова (Медиазона) 2016).

objects.description: An attempted armed seizure of power in the spring of 2014 by storming regional administrations: the UN recorded that already "in mid-April 2014" "groups of armed men unlawfully carried out a well-organized and coordinated seizure of public buildings and police and security service offices in towns and villages of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions," and "in order to retain control of the seized areas these groups set up barricades and checkpoints"(Citation: Доклад Верховного комиссара ООН по правам человека о положении в области прав человека в Украине (A/HRC/27/75) 2014). In Kharkiv the coup was quickly suppressed.

objects.description: The instigation of armed clashes in Odesa on May 2, 2014: the UN records the violence committed "in Odesa on 2 May 2014 during clashes between supporters of unity and supporters of the federalization of Ukraine, as a result of which 48 people died, mostly supporters of the country's federalization," and notes that "no one has yet been held to account"(Citation: Доклад Верховного комиссара ООН по правам человека о положении в области прав человека в Украине (A/HRC/27/75) 2014). The culmination was the fire in the Trade Union Building where activists had taken refuge: the UN monitoring mission listed among the key uninvestigated questions "what caused the fire in the Trade Union building" and "who are the perpetrators of the killings"(Citation: Report on the human rights situation in Ukraine, 15 June 2014 (OHCHR) 2014).

objects.description: The exploitation of the Odesa tragedy to build a state propaganda myth and invert the roles: the actual picture, per the UN, is clashes "between supporters of unity and supporters of the federalization of Ukraine, as a result of which 48 people died," while the investigation remains incomplete and "no one has yet been held to account"(Citation: Доклад Верховного комиссара ООН по правам человека о положении в области прав человека в Украине (A/HRC/27/75) 2014). The tragedy was used as moral justification for further aggression - by the same device as the "crucified boy" fake, for which "there is no evidence to support Pyshniak's claim"(Citation: Fake: Crucifixion in Slovyansk 2014).

objects.description: The publication of the manifesto "On the Historical Unity of Russians and Ukrainians" (July 2021), constructing a pseudo-historical myth: "Russians and Ukrainians are one people, a single whole," while modern borders are declared the result of the fact that "the Bolsheviks' actions in severing from Russia its historical territories are not considered a criminal act"(Citation: Статья Владимира Путина «Об историческом единстве русских и украинцев» 2021). The same article describes how Lenin personally "persuaded" the leaders of the Donetsk-Kryvyi Rih republic "to act within Soviet Ukraine," and how the Central Committee resolved "to create at the congress 'one government for all of Ukraine'"(Citation: Статья Владимира Путина «Об историческом единстве русских и украинцев» 2021). On the eve of the invasion the thesis was taken to its limit: in his address of February 21, 2022 Putin declared that "modern Ukraine was entirely and wholly created by Russia, or, to be more precise, by Bolshevik, communist Russia," and called the country "Ukraine named after Vladimir Ilyich Lenin" - "He is its author and architect"(Citation: Обращение Президента Российской Федерации 21 февраля 2022 года 2022).
